description: Celestia is a pluggable consensus and data availability layer for blockchains and decentralised apps. By making the base layer as simple as possible, Celestia is enabling as much versatility as possible for developers building on top of it. While current blockchains are considered monolithic, which simply means that transaction execution, blockchain consensus, and data availability are processed and maintained on the same blockchain. name: Altibbi
description: Altibbi is the leading digital health platform in the Arab world, providing telemedicine consultations, and medical content. It connects patients with certified doctors and offers 24/7 remote healthcare services. The platform aims to improve healthcare accessibility across MENA.. The digital health platform has 192M+ users with millions of consultations and recommendations provided annually.

name: Anghami
description: Anghami is the leading music and audio streaming platform in the MENA region, offering Arabic and international content across music, podcasts, and entertainment. It operates a freemium model with premium subscriptions and strategic partnerships with telcos. The company is publicly listed on NASDAQ following its SPAC merger. The MENA music platform has 120M+ users, 3.5M+ subscribers, and ~$48M H1 revenue across 16 markets.

name: Basma
description: Basma is a healthtech company specializing in digital orthodontics, offering at-home teeth straightening solutions supported by remote monitoring. It combines telehealth with customized treatment plans. Basma aims to make orthodontic care more accessible and affordable.

name: Bevy (Previously Eventtus)
description: Bevy is a community management platform that enables brands to build, manage, and scale global communities through events and engagement tools. It evolved from Eventtus into a broader SaaS platform supporting virtual, hybrid, and in-person events. Bevy serves enterprises looking to drive customer engagement.

name: Bykea
description: Bykea is a ride-hailing and logistics platform in Pakistan offering bike rides, deliveries, and payments services. It leverages a large network of riders to provide affordable mobility and last-mile delivery. The platform targets mass-market urban users. The Super app has 5M users and 1.7M monthly active users in Pakistan.

name: Clinicy
description: Clinicy is a healthcare SaaS platform that provides clinics and medical practices with digital tools for patient management, scheduling, and electronic medical records. It streamlines clinic operations and improves patient experience. The platform targets small to mid-sized healthcare providers. Healthcare SaaS driving 2M SAR Annual Revenue Recovered (532,800 USD) for clinics.

name: Cognitev (previously MENA Commerce)
description: Cognitev is an AI-powered advertising technology company that enables automated media buying and campaign optimization. It leverages machine learning to improve ad performance across digital channels. The company operates globally with a focus on performance marketing with 150+ professionals and 6 innovation initiatives.

name: Cookpad (previously Shahiya)
description: Cookpad is a global recipe-sharing platform that enables users to discover and share home-cooked meals. Shahiya was its leading Arabic platform prior to acquisition. The platform monetizes through subscriptions and community-driven content.

name: Designer 24
description: Designer-24 is a luxury fashion rental platform in the Middle East (UAE, Lebanon, and Jordan) that makes high-end designer clothing accessible to women. It offers curated, on-trend looks for various occasions while promoting sustainability and women empowerment by reducing the need for fast fashion purchases.

name: Dixio
description: Dixio is a fintech infrastructure company providing API-based connectivity between financial institutions, corporates, and payment systems. Its platform enables secure, standardized messaging and integration across banking networks. Dixio focuses on simplifying financial data exchange and interoperability. Cross-border payments infrastructure serving 200+ clients across 60+ countries.

name: Eat
description: Eat is a restaurant technology platform providing POS systems, reservations, and customer management solutions for the hospitality industry. It helps restaurants digitize operations and improve customer engagement. Eat covers 90+ countries, 5K+ restaurants, and 80+ hotel groups.

name: Erad
description: Erad is a fintech that specializes in providing financial solutions for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in KSA and UAE

name: Fadel
description: Fadel is a rights and royalty management software provider for media, publishing, and entertainment industries. Its platform enables companies to manage intellectual property rights, contracts, and revenue distribution. Fadel serves global enterprise clients reducing their processing time by 50% and asset clearance time by 70%.

name: FlapKap
description: FlapKap is a fintech platform providing revenue-based financing solutions to e-commerce and digital businesses. It enables merchants to access non-dilutive capital based on their sales performance. The platform uses data integrations to underwrite and deploy funding quickly.

name: Fresha
description: Fresha is a global SaaS marketplace for beauty and wellness businesses, offering booking, payments, and customer management tools. It operates a commission-free model for merchants while monetizing through payments and add-ons. Fresha serves millions of users across salons and spas worldwide. Global beauty & wellness platform powering 130K+ businesses and 1B+ bookings across 120+ countries.

name: Fundbot
description: Fundbot is a supply chain financing platform that provides SMEs with working capital by financing invoices and purchase orders. It leverages alternative data and fintech infrastructure to improve credit access. The platform connects businesses, lenders, and financial institutions.

name: Hala
description: Hala is an SME-focused fintech providing digital payment solutions, including POS systems, payment acceptance, and business management tools—enabling small merchants to seamlessly accept and manage transactions. The SME-focused fintech processes $6B+ in transactions with 100K users and is licensed by SAMA.

name: HyperPay
description: HyperPay is a payment gateway platform in MENA enabling businesses to accept online payments securely. It supports multiple payment methods and provides fraud protection and analytics tools. The company serves e-commerce and enterprise clients processing 2,400+ TPS across 10K+ merchants in 9 countries.

name: Invygo

description: When you look at Ninja Van today, with over 30,000 employees in six markets, delivering over 1000+ parcels per minute, you would not think that back in 2014, founders Chang Wen, Tan Bo Xian and Shaun Chong were just three guys sleeping on mattresses on the floor of their office trying to solve one of the most hairy and complex inefficiencies in Southeast Asia - last-mile logistics.

name: NOVI Health
description: NOVI Health is a technology-enabled healthcare company that provides hyper-personalized holistic health solutions integrating precision medicine, behavioral and lifestyle interventions, to prevent and better manage chronic conditions such as diabetes, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, fatty liver and obesity.‍

name: Openexus
description: Openexus builds a platform and community for universal modular building blocks for the Internet.

name: Ordinary Folk
description: Ordinary Folk reimagines the building blocks of healthcare in Asia.

name: Padlet
description: Built on the premise that much of daily work is actually storytelling, Padlet provides stunning visuals and varied functionality to help users express ideas creatively, while collaborating with others in a fun manner.

name: Proptech Builders
description: Proptech Builders is building an ecosystem of AI-powered PropTech ventures to tackle the Southeast Asian property market and unlock $21 trillion in trapped wealth.

name: Radiant1
description: Radiant 1 is a hotel industry-focused big data company providing revenue management services through the help of AI and Machine Learning.

name: Rainforest
description: Rainforest is Asia’s leading e-commerce brand aggregator.

name: Saladin
description: Saladin is an one-touch insurance platform, incorporating a multi-channel distribution system powered by technology.

name: Stellar
description: Stellar helps build and scale companies efficiently, and is designed to take the complexity, research and guesswork out of compliance, financial and people operations, and grow a business every step of the way.

name: Tigerhall
description: Tigerhall is the only platform built for Chief Transformation Officers to execute large-scale transformation strategies effectively. It centralizes everything needed to activate change strategies—automating change communications, capability building, and real-time progress tracking in one system—so transformation teams can drive faster results while saving time and resources.

name: twoplus Fertility
description: Hannah Life Technologies/twoplus Fertility provides accessible and affordable solutions for the fertility health space.

name: UIlicious
description: UIlicious is a software testing automation platform that allows software teams to effortlessly test and monitor end-to-test user journeys for their web applications across browsers.

name: URBANMETRY
description: Leading Malaysia-based data analytics company enhancing property data quality across developing Asia. Using AI and proprietary algorithms, Urbanmetry harvests, cleans, and analyzes city data to extract crucial urban trends and patterns. This approach empowers governments to make informed decisions, thereby improving city planning, and promoting sustainable urban environments.

name: VuCar
description: VuCar is a C2B marketplace revolutionizing the used car industry in Vietnam, Laos, and Cambodia.

name: エスマット（旧：スマートショッピング）
エネコートテクノロジーズ
ADB Airfield Solutions
description: The market leader in airfield lighting, which is critical infrastructure for the aviation industry. ADB designs, manufactures and services innovative lighting products and systems for airfield operations around the world.  It was a non-core division of Siemens and we carved-out the business in 2009.

name: Aqua Lung
description: The leading manufacturer of branded diving equipment for recreational and professional use. Aqualung has successfully diversified from its expertise in scuba diving into several other aquatic equipment markets, including swimming, free diving, and snorkeling.

name: Arkopharma
description: A leading developer and manufacturer of products including natural therapies, vitamins and minerals, medical and beauty products and are sold mainly to pharmacists and health and wellness retail stores.

name: Artemis
description: Artemis is a leading private medical eye care clinic group and a leading provider of ophthalmic care in Germany. Founded in 1999, the group originally operated mainly in Hesse and North Rhine-Westphalia and has since expanded, through a combination of organic growth and acquisition, to operate across Germany.

name: BSN Medical
description: A leading global producer of medical supplies, operating in three key segments: Traditional and Advanced Wound Care, Compression Therapy, and Orthopaedics. The company was founded in 2001 as a joint venture between Beiersdorf and Smith & Nephew and we originally carved out BSN Medical in 2006. We then reinvested as a minority shareholder until 2017.

name: CAP
description: The UK’s leading provider of vehicle valuation data and related services. CAP’s data and the ubiquitous CAPCode taxonomy are the industry benchmarks and critical infrastructure in the UK market for transacting and owning vehicles. We acquired the business in May 2012 as a carve-out from the EMAP Group.

name: CliniSys
description: The leading provider of Laboratory Information Management Systems to clinical laboratories across Europe. CliniSys provides software to manage the key workflows within, and between, clinical laboratories. This enables laboratories to perform and process tests in a timely, efficient and automated manner and to communicate the results to relevant care providers.

name: ClinPhone
description: A leading specialist supplier of technology solutions to the clinical trials industry. Montagu first invested in ClinPhone alongside a co-investor in 1996, which helped the business develop into a global business providing integrated technology solutions for clinical trials to most of the largest pharmaceutical companies worldwide. In 2006, Montagu exited its investment through an Initial Public Offering on the London Stock Exchange.

name: Cory Environmental
description: One of the UK’s leading waste management companies and was best known for operating barges on the River Thames. In April 2005, Montagu Private Equity led the management buyout of Cory Environmental. Cory Environmental was a 100% owned subsidiary of Exel, plc, whose main business was logistics and supply chain management. Montagu was attracted to Cory because of its contracted revenue streams, well-placed landfill sites and its very experienced and highly regarded management team. In March 2007 Montagu sold Cory to a consortium of long-term infrastructure investors consisting of ABN AMRO Global Infrastructure Fund (ABN AMRO GIF), Finpro SGPS and Santander Private Equity, on behalf of Santander Infrastructure Funds I and II.

name: DAVASO
description: Germany’s largest provider of tech-enabled claims processing, invoice auditing and billing preparation services for statutory health insurers. DAVASO’s software solutions are used to improve its internal operations as well as by other service providers to automate their own processes.

name: DEAS Group
description: The leading provider of property management and adjacent services to property owners in the Danish market. DEAS offers a full range of property and asset management services to large institutional and smaller private investors, as well as housing associations.

name: Dignity
description: The UK’s largest funeral services company, conducting around 70,000 funerals per annum from a network of over 500 funeral homes and operating 21 crematoria. In February 2002 Montagu led the management buyout of Dignity Funeral Services from Houston-based Service Corporation International (“SCI”). The strengths of our proposal, our relationship with management and our reputation for delivery gave SCI the confidence to award us exclusivity in January. We completed the transaction five weeks later. In April 2004 Dignity returned to the London Stock Exchange following a successful IPO, which valued the business at £394 million.

name: DORC
description: A leading provider of surgical equipment, consumables, instruments, and liquids used in vitreoretinal surgery. DORC has a range of products closely developed with surgeons including: A leading provider of surgical equipment, consumables, instruments, and liquids used in vitreoretinal surgery. DORC has a range of products closely developed with surgeons including:

name: Emitel
description: The leading owner and operator of nationwide tower infrastructure in Poland. Emitel offers business-critical services to TV and radio broadcasters and transmission services for mobile operators.

name: Equatex
description: A deferred compensation services provider, specialising in the design, implementation and administration of deferred equity plans. Equatex’s customers include large global corporates across different industries including pharmaceuticals, engineering, financial services, consumer products and software. The company was initially set up to serve internal UBS deferred compensation plans but expanded to serve external clients. We acquired it in 2015 as a carve-out from UBS.

name: Eudonet Group
description: A leading and specialised CRM business focused on niche verticals including charities, government & local authorities and higher education.

name: Euromedic International
description: The largest pan-European medical service provider specialising in diagnostics imaging and cancer care services.

name: Evergen
description: Premier CDMO in regenerative medicine offering a comprehensive portfolio of allograft and xenograft biomaterials at scale.

name: EXALTA
description: EXALTA is the strategic merger of Tyber Medical (new acquisition), Intech Medical (MVI portfolio company) and Resolve Surgical Technologies (MV portfolio company), creating a global leader in orthopaedic contract design and manufacturing. Completed in April 2025, EXALTA combines expertise across trauma, spine, extremities, sports medicine, and robotic-assisted surgery, offering a unique breadth of capabilities and faster innovation. Its vertically integrated platform enhances supply-chain speed, resilience, and simplicity, enabling 2/3 faster speed-to-market compared to competitors.

name: Funeral Partners
description: Funeral Partners, founded in 2007, is the third largest funeral services provider in the UK. It operates through a network of local funeral homes that retain their individual brands and heritage. Montagu acquired a majority stake in 2016, in partnership with management.

name: Galileo Global Education
description: Founded in 2009 and headquartered in Paris, Galileo is Europe’s largest higher education group, in terms of both geographical spread and breadth of courses offered. We invested in Galileo in 2020 as part of a consortium of institutional investors.

name: Hansen Protection
description: A leading provider of survival suits used in transport between land and offshore installations and personal protection suits for marine and hazardous environments. Hansen Protection (previously Helly Hansen Survival) was founded in 1995 as part of the Helly Hansen Group and we carved it out in 2011 allowing it to focus on its professional niche.

name: Harvest
description: Harvest provides a SaaS software platform to 4,900+ clients and is one of the leading European wealth management software solutions, serving independent financial advisers, asset managers, private and retail banks, and insurers, amongst others. It supports their entire customer journey, including client management and engagement, wealth and tax planning, data and investment strategy and subscription. It operates a subscription-based software business model, complemented by recurring consumption-based products and the implementation and servicing of its solutions.

name: Host Europe
description: A leading provider of web hosting and domain registration services to SMEs and individual customers in the UK and Germany. Host Europe Group (“Host Europe”) was founded in 1997 and operates under the “webfusion” and “123-reg” brands in the UK and the “Host Europe” brand in Germany. Montagu established a close relationship with the management, and a clear understanding of the business and were then offered exclusivity in October 2010.

name: HTL Biotechnology
description: The world leader in the development and production of innovative, pharmaceutical-grade biopolymers used by top pharmaceutical and medical device companies to transform the lives of millions of patients in multiple therapeutic areas such as ophthalmology, dermatology, medical aesthetics, rheumatology, and urology.

name: IAI Group
description: Founded in 2000, IAI is Poland’s leading digital retail solutions provider, enabling mid-to-large size merchants in Poland and Central and Eastern Europe to build tailored e-commerce operations. The Company’s flagship product, Idosell, is a comprehensive proprietary technology platform that powers individual merchants end-to-end online operations.

name: IMV Technologies
description: IMV Technologies is the world leader in animal artificial insemination, embryo transfer and veterinary imaging.

name: INGENYX
description: INGENYX (formerly Teleflex Medical OEM) is a leading contract developer and manufacturer of custom-engineered interventional catheter components and sub-assemblies, as well as surgical fibers and sutures. With seven sites across the U.S., Mexico, and Ireland, the Company combines deep materials expertise with vertically integrated manufacturing and dedicated EPIC design centers to help customers bring high-performance medical devices to market.

name: ISI Markets
description: ISI Markets is the leading provider of macroeconomic data, industry, company and sovereign intelligence.

name: ITRS Group
description: ITRS Group is a leading global provider of IT operations monitoring and analytics software for the “always on” enterprise, used by >3,000 clients globally to manage their operations and ensure operational resilience.

name: Janes
description: A leading provider of open source intelligence, providing timely information and data for industries including aerospace, defence, and security. Montagu completed the acquisition of Janes from IHS Markit in December 2019.

name: Lighteum Medical
description: Lighteum Medical develops and manufactures critical and complex miniature components for minimally invasive medical devices used in high-growth clinical specialties. It focuses on complex and high-precision components made from Platinum Group Metals and Nitinol, with decades of expertise in the metallurgy, micromachining, and advanced Nitinol processing.

name: Lloyd’s List Intelligence
description: Provider of market-leading products offering reliable, high-quality maritime data and actionable analytics, with mission-critical applications across compliance, risk management and operations.

name: Maincare
description: Provider of software for French public hospitals and state-run health authorities. Maincare addresses the critical software needs of health organisations through an integrated suite of products spanning electronic patient records, population health solutions, and back-office tools.

name: Marlow Foods
description: A manufacturer of an extensive range of branded chilled and frozen ingredients and meals from its manufacturing base in north Yorkshire. Quorn was the UK’s number one brand in the fast-growing healthy meat alternative food segment with an established and successful presence in a number of European territories. Montagu led the buyout of Marlow Foods, the owner of Quorn-branded food products, in the first half of 2003 from AstraZeneca. Following our acquisition of the business, Marlow Foods performed strongly in its core European territories and grew rapidly in the US from a standing start in 2002. In June 2005 we sold Marlow Foods to Premier Foods Plc.

name: Miraclon
description: One of the world’s leading providers of imaging technologies for the graphics customisation of printed packaging materials. Montagu completed the acquisition of Kodak’s Flexographic Packaging Division in April 2019. Shortly after the transaction closed, the business was renamed “Miraclon”. Miraclon’s flagship flexographic plate imaging system, FLEXCEL NX, has received industry-wide acclaim for its leading image resolution quality, since debuting on the market in 2008. Flexography is the most common form of packaging printing and can apply images on almost any substrate, with a speciality in flexible packaging.

name: Multifonds
description: Multifonds, founded in 1995 in Luxembourg, is a global provider of proprietary investment accounting and transfer agency software used to perform a range of back- and middle-office fund services tasks. The platform supports over 40,000 funds and more than $10 trillion in assets across 35+ jurisdictions.

name: Nemera
description: A proven, rapidly growing producer of complex drug delivery systems. Nemera designs and manufactures a full range of drug delivery systems including asthma inhalers, insulin pens, auto-injectors and nasal pumps. The Nemera Group originally comprised two businesses at acquisition in May 2014: a healthcare devices business (Nemera) as well as a prescription retail containers and closures business (Centor, which was sold in 2015), both carved-out of Rexam plc. In January 2019, we reinvested in Nemera alongside another investor to support the next phase of Nemera’s growth.

name: OASIS Group
description: A European provider of records and information management services across the UK, Ireland, the Netherlands, Poland and Belgium. OASIS’s services allow its customers to manage their records holistically and cost-effectively across the entire document lifecycle and help ensure regulatory compliance.

name: Open GI
description: A provider of state-of-the-art, mission-critical broker software, and services to the UK & Ireland general insurance market. Open GI’s software facilitates brokers and insurers to write personal and commercial insurance. Founded in 1979, we acquired the business for a second time in 2014 having invested in Open GI between 2006 and 2007.

name: ParentPay Group
description: The combination of ESS, a leading provider of administrative software solutions for the UK education sector, and ParentPay, a leading provider of online school payments and parental engagement solutions, creating a leading EdTech platform serving schools across the UK and Europe.

name: Risdon Pharma
description: A leading European manufacturer of primary plastic packaging for the pharmaceutical industry. Risdon Pharma was the European leader in blow moulded containers such as eye droppers and nasal sprays, and a major player in the fast-growing segment of drug delivery systems, such as metered dosage anti-asthma inhalers. In March 2002, Montagu acquired Risdon Pharma from Crown Cork and Seal Inc. (“Crown”) for €97 million. Following an approach from a number of interested trade acquirors, in August 2003 the company was sold to Rexam Plc. The success of this transaction was based upon the robust commitment shown by the management team to lead their own buyout. We gave them the support they needed to make the deal happen and built an understanding that allowed us together to make the key strategic decisions that underpinned the value increase in the business and subsequent exit. In 2014 we partnered again with the management team in the carve-out transaction of Nemera , formally Rexam’s Healthcare Devices division.

name: Sebia
description: A global leader in the diagnostics of serum protein with a superior technology in electrophoresis. Sebia is a research-driven company covering several pathologies including multiple myeloma, diabetes (HbA1c) and haemoglobin deficiencies. Montagu originally acquired the business in 2006 and invested for a second time in 2014.

name: Servelec
description: A provider of healthcare and case management software to NHS trusts and local authorities. Servelec has a focus in mental health, community care and interoperability and Montagu acquired it in January 2018 in a take-private transaction.

name: Stabilus
description: A market-leading manufacturer of gas springs, hydraulic vibration dampers, continuously adjustable doorstays and automatic opening and closing systems for doors, trunk lids and tailgates. Stabilus’s diversified customer base with long standing and close customer relationships, its unrivalled market position and strong management team made it an ideal investment for Montagu. In August 2004 Montagu led the Management Buyout of Stabilus, at that time a subsidiary of Demag Sarl a conglomerate owned by KKR and Siemens. In May 2008 Stabilus was sold to Paine & Partners, LLC, US-based private equity firm.

name: Steam Packet Company
description: Montagu led the Management Buyout in July 2003 from Sea Containers. The Steam Packet Company had a dominant position in the transportation of passengers and freight to the Isle of Man from ports in the UK underpinned by a long-standing user agreement with the Isle of Man government. The Steam Packet represented a very high quality, secure and cash generative business growing in line with a robust Manx economy. These features made it ideal for a leveraged buyout and as such our success in buying this business was at the end of a fiercely fought private equity auction. In October 2005 Montagu sold the Isle of Man Steam Packet Company to Macquarie Bank.

name: Survitec
description: The world’s leading survival technology company focused on serving the marine, military, aerospace and homeland security markets. In August 2004, Montagu led the Management Buyout of The Survitec Group, a division of Air-Sea Survival Equipment Limited, which was controlled by the Alchemy Investment Plan. We backed the management team with follow on capital to both make further acquisitions and to fund the move of some of its manufacturing into low cost territories. In February 2010, Survitec was sold to Warburg Pincus.

name: The University of Law
description: The leading provider of professional legal education and training in England and Wales. The University of Law focused principally on the provision of post-graduate legal training through the Legal Practice Course (LPC) and the Graduate Diploma in Law (GDL). The business was founded in 1962 and was originally set up as a not-for-profit Royal Charter charitable corporation. It was known as the College of Law until 2012 but it was awarded University status following our investment.

name: Ultra Electronics
description: Ultra Electronics is a group of businesses that manage a portfolio of specialist capabilities, generating highly differentiated solutions and products in the defence & aerospace, security & cyber, transport and energy markets by applying electronic and software technologies in demanding and critical environments to meet customer needs. Montagu backed the management buy-out of seven businesses of the Dowty Electronics Systems Division of Dowty Group in 1993 and was made public on the London Stock Exchange in 1996.

name: Universal Investment
description: Universal Investment is a European third-party management company (“ManCo”) and fund administration service provider, serving institutional investors and asset managers. Founded in 1968 as a joint venture of German private banks, it was owned by Berenberg and Bankhaus Lampe before Montagu acquired it in a carve-out in January 2017.

name: VetXX
description: Marketer of pharmaceutical products for skin, eye and ear diseases, and producer of pet diet food (through the brand SPECIFIC) and pet care products for companion animals. VetXX’s animal health products were distributed exclusively through veterinary surgeries in more than 35 countries. In March 2005, Montagu led and arranged the Management Buyout of Leo Animal Health (subsequently renamed VetXX) from its shareholder, the privately owned Danish pharmaceutical company Leo Pharma. In December 2007 VetXX was sold to Dechra Pharmaceuticals.

name: Visma
description: A provider of business management software in Northern Europe. Visma provides mission-critical financial, accounting, payroll and HR software primarily to SMEs and public sector organisations. Montagu was involved with Visma from its first minority investment in 2010, reinvestment in 2014 and again in 2017.

name: Volution
description: A leading supplier of ventilation products that, at the time of our investment, included Vent-Axia (ventilation), Kopex and Adaptaflex (ducting and fittings for electrical cables). In December 2002 Montagu led the Management Buyout of Smiths Group plc’s building products division, which was renamed Volution Holdings Limited. At the time of our approach, Smiths was considering separate disposals of its air movement and cable management divisions. We saw that both divisions were under common management and serving common customers and we approached Smiths Group with an offer for both divisions. This approach simplified the disposal for the vendor and had the support of management who had plans for both product groups. In May 2003 Volution disposed of Airstream, its washroom rentals division and in August 2006 Volution was sold to ABN AMRO Capital, the private equity arm of ABN AMRO.

name: Waystone Group
description: A leading provider of management company, fund governance, fund administration, risk and compliance services to the asset management industry.

name: Wireless Logic
description: Wireless Logic is the leading independent global Internet of Things (“IoT”) connectivity platform provider. It delivers a critical IoT network infrastructure platform, enabling 25,000+ customers to “connect”, “control” and “secure” over 20 million devices across 165 countries to over 750 global networks.

name: Adjuvance
description: Shingles is a painful disease that is estimated to afflict 1 in 3 adults over their lifetime. GSK has developed Shingrix into a $2b+ vaccine franchise, but its superior activity comes from the QS21 adjuvant, which is in extremely short supply due to its natural origin. Adjuvance has developed a semi-synthetic process for mass-producing a superior version of QS21; this adjuvant is expected to enhance vaccines where efficacy is less than optimal.

name: Alamar Bio

Its fully automated, high-throughput precision proteomics platform will pave the way to discovering the deepest secrets of the proteome. It has the potential to fulfill the promise of the human plasma proteome to transform healthcare with a new wave of biomarkers for early detection and prevention of common diseases.

name: Alentis Therapeutics

name: Almond FinTech

name: Apellis
description: Complement-mediated disorders stem from overactive innate immune activity. Apellis is developing an injectable peptide therapy that inhibits the C3 complement protein in diseases like paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria, C3 glomerulopathy, geographic atrophy of the eye, and cold agglutinin disease. C3 inhibition reduces the severity of symptoms that C5 inhibition does not affect. Apellis recently announced positive Phase 3 data in PNH and are looking to advance trials in many other complement disorders.

name: Biothea

name: Blue Onion Labs

name: Blueberry Pediatrics

name: Cairn Surgical
description: Cairn Surgical is developing a personalized guide for breast cancer surgery, a procedure that treads a fine line between sparing breast tissue and cancer-free surgical margins. Proprietary algorithms translate imaging into a 3D mold that ensures clean margins with minimal tissue loss. The technology is currently undergoing clinical trials.

name: Canopy Immuno-Therapeutics
description: Canopy Immuno-Therapeutics is developing a novel class of antigen-specific biologics through its “Reverse Immunization” platform with the goal of eliminating pathogenic immune responses in autoimmune disorders and severe allergies, without broadly suppressing the immune system. www.canopy-biotech.com

name: Casana
description: Casana is re-inventing in-home health monitoring technologies that provide clinicians with access to reliable, consistent vital signs to do what is best for their patients. The Heart Seat™ passively captures health parameters such as blood pressure, ejection fraction, and oxygen saturation via sensors embedded in a toilet seat, enabling data collection with no change in patient behavior. By collecting these parameters longitudinally, Casana gives clinicians an accurate picture of where a patient is on their heart health journey and can notify them early if intervention is needed.

name: CellCentric
description: London-based CellCentric has developed a first-in-class small-molecule inhibitor of histone acetyltransferases (p300/CBP) that are key co-regulators of transcriptional activity. Certain cancers over-express these two regulators, and inhibition with this drug class has shown strong results in prostate cancer, heme indications like multiple myeloma and non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma, and in AR- or c-Myc dependent cancers. CellCentric has initiated clinical studies in both prostate and heme cancers.

description: There are an estimated 250 million chronic carriers of Hepatitis B virus worldwide. Patients with this infection are at risk for liver cirrhosis, cancer, and death. Cognito has developed a device that administers visual and audio stimulation in this frequency range that is being tested in clinical trials for the symptoms of Alzheimer’s disease.

name: Eko Devices
description: Eko combines enhanced audio, medical-grade ECG, and AI-powered analysis to affectively detect cardiac conditions and provide timely care from anywhere. name: Geneoscopy
description: Colorectal cancer is the second-leading cause of cancer deaths annually in the United States and early detection and treatment are key to improve survival. Geneoscopy is a clinical-stage diagnostics company focused on new methods for early detection of gastrointestinal diseases and cancer. Geneoscopy has developed a proprietary isolation and screening platform to assay RNA biomarkers from stool. This platform is non-invasive and can be used by patients at home. The initial diagnostic focuses on early detection of colorectal neoplasms and advanced adenomas in average-risk individuals and was granted Breakthrough Device Designation by the US FDA in January 2020. Geneoscopy’s findings from its initial clinical study demonstrated 95% sensitivity with traditional colonoscopy-based screenings for detecting colorectal cancer.

name: GreenLight Bio

name: MedAnnex

description: Music as Medicine MedRhythms is a digital therapeutics company that uses sensors, music, and software to build evidence-based, neurologic interventions to affect a variety of conditions. The company leverages the ability of music to directly stimulate the brain, resulting in neurological entrainment across the organ. Follow-on indications include multiple sclerosis, Parkinson’s Disease, acute stroke, and Alzheimer’s Disease. name: Mesentech

name: MeVox
description: Falling coverage, waning immunity, and non-vaccine genotypes have led to a resurgence in mumps and measles cases worldwide. The current MMR shot is a live viral vaccine, and thus performs poorly as a booster shot. MeVox is developing a stabilized measles and mumps booster shot that locks antigens in their most immunogenic conformations, eliciting a robust response from a durable booster shot.

name: Neuroelectrics
description: Neuroelectrics has developed a proprietary algorithm that uses both EEG data and MRI scans to map individualized brain circuits and deliver customized transcranial electric stimulation therapy to affected regions. The technology is in clinical trials for treatment-resistant epilepsy, of which there are 500,000 patients in the US alone. The Neuroelectrics headset and software platform is also being tested in trials for depression, ADHD, and Alzheimer’s Disease.

name: Neutrolis
description: Neutrolis is developing first-in-class therapies for autoimmune and inflammatory diseases by targeting Neutrophil Extracellular Traps (NETs), a fundamental arm of the innate immune system which plays an important role in chronic and acute diseases. Neutrolis employs the exDNASE platform, based on naturally occurring enzymes that degrade the extracellular chromatin that form NETs, and powers the creation of natural and engineered enzyme analogs that are capable of treating several acute and chronic unmet medical needs. The lead candidate NTR-441 is an enhanced analog of DNASE1L3, an enzyme produced by immune cells that degrades NETs into biologically inactive fragments to attenuate a severe immune response. The company’s pipeline includes NTR-441, systemically active engineered DNASE1L3, and NTR-452, locally active engineered DNASE1L3, that effectively removes NETs and halt their pathologic effects.

name: Nocion Therapeutics
description: Nocion Therapeutics develops “nocions” — charged small-molecule sodium-channel blockers designed to selectively silence activated nociceptors while sparing normal sensory pathways. The company’s lead program, Taplucainium, is advancing in a global Phase 2b trial for refractory chronic cough, addressing a high-unmet medical need with a differentiated mechanism. www.nociontx.com

name: Origin Medical
description: Origin Medical develops AI technology that assists clinicians in performing and interpreting pregnancy ultrasound scans with greater confidence and consistency. Its device-agnostic platform integrates medical expertise with advanced imaging workflows to help identify high-risk pregnancies early, support timely interventions, and reduce maternal and infant mortality. name: Vigeo
description: Vigeo has developed a first-in-class drug discovery pipeline that reprograms the tumor microenvironment (TME). The lead compound stimulates the expression of thrombospondin, which has a downstream inhibitory effect on CD36 and CD47, commonly known as the “don’t-eat-me” signal. Expression of this protein in the TME turns “cold” tumors “hot” by increasing immune trafficking into the TME and reducing suppressive cell populations. Vigeo has begun Phase 1 clinical trials and expects interim results from expansion cohorts in mid-2020.

name: Advanced Navigation
description: Advanced Navigation is a Sydney-based developer of Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) systems that provide users with highly accurate positioning data, even in environments where GPS signals are jammed, spoofed or unavailable. Founded in 2012, the company has since deployed over 100,000 systems to a global customer base.

name: Advemto
description: Advemto has developed, and demonstrated, a breakthrough technology for improving the measurement of fluorescent markers used across life sciences. The company is applying this core IP to Smart Plates: a consumable that links immune cell behaviour to genetic identity at single-cell scale, without requiring customers to purchase any new hardware.

name: Alimetry
description: Alimetry has developed diagnostic technology for gastric dysfunction, aiming to provide an “EKG for the stomach.” Its first product is a non-invasive wearable device that uses 64 electrodes to measure stomach muscle activity, with results transmitted wirelessly for clinician analysis and visualisation.

name: Atomic.io
description: Atomic.io is a low-code platform enabling enterprises to deliver highly personalised, interactive in-app messages securely and at scale. From nudging customers through key decisions to rewarding milestones and replacing costly SMS, the platform turns a company’s app into its most trusted and impactful communication channel.

name: Auror
description: Auror provides a crime intelligence system to brick-and-mortar retailers, used by front-line store employees, headquarters staff and the police to help prevent organised crime, reduce loss from theft and make stores feel safer for employees.

name: AutoGrab
description: AutoGrab is an Australian based automotive intelligence platform that provides real-time data and insights to dealers, insurers, lenders, and fleet operators, by offering a suite of products including live pricing, vehicle sourcing, inventory management, pre-accident valuations and fleet management.

name: Avasa
description: Avasa is a groundbreaking MedTech startup founded by surgeon-turned-bioengineer Dr. Nandoun Abeysekera, who developed a novel tubular tissue transformer to automate and standardise microvascular surgery procedures, specifically arterial anastomosis. This technology is poised to disrupt the current manual method, offering clinicians a precise, easy-to-adopt tool to improve patient clinical outcomes with minimal upskilling required.

name: B.Spkl
description: B.Spkl is developing a novel method for producing high-performance, low-cost catalysts, initially targeting the hydrogen electrolyser market. By using a single-stage process to vastly simplify the catalyst manufacturing process, the company creates significant cost savings and enables a more cost-effective and scalable production of clean Hydrogen.

name: Basis
description: With increased EVs, solar, and home energy electrification seen across the world, Basis developed a new smart panel, designed to replace traditional residential switchboards with a digital system that gives homeowners real-time visibility and control over their energy usage, modernising how household electricity is managed, improving safety and efficiency, and allowing faster installation compared to conventional switchboards.

name: Cadmus Animal Health
description: Cadmus Animal Health is a New Zealand-based company developing an immunotherapeutic for periodontal disease in companion animals. Rather than cleaning and extraction once damage is done, it trains the animal's immune system against the Porphyromonas bacteria that drive the disease. The company spun out of Denteric, a human health company built on University of Melbourne research into the same bacteria.

name: Crimson Education
description: Crimson Education was founded in 2013 with a focus on university admissions, and quickly expanded into a broader platform supporting high-performing students across their education journey. At its core is technology that enables personalised, data-driven learning and support at scale, informed by a growing dataset and consistently strong outcomes.

name: Dawn Aerospace
description: Dawn Aerospace is creating next-generation space transportation with a focus on building eco-friendly satellite propulsion systems and reusable spaceplane technology. It has become the world's leading supplier of green in-space propulsion, with more than 200 thrusters flown across 50-plus satellites. Its Mk-II Aurora, a rocket-powered suborbital spaceplane, is the first privately developed aircraft to fly supersonic since Concorde and is now taking commercial orders.

name: Evnex
description: Evnex produces AC (Alternating Current) electric vehicle chargers for homes and workplaces, paired with interoperable software that enables electricity distributors to dynamically manage when chargers draw power from the network. They currently facilitate the largest network of residential and workplace chargers in NZ and have relationships with more than ten electricity distributors including Vector and Powerco.

name: Fleet Space Technologies
description: Fleet Space Technologies is an Australian company building the leading platform for mineral exploration. It pairs proprietary satellite and sensor technology with an AI model to produce 3D subsurface models in hours rather than months, improving outcomes and lowering environmental impact for miners. The technology also extends to defence and space.

name: Hnry
description: Founded in 2017, Hnry is an all-in-one financial platform for sole traders, integrating payments, banking, accounting tools, and professional accountancy across New Zealand, Australia, and the United Kingdom. Beyond tax, it streamlines end-to-end financial administration across 300+ verticals through a fully integrated, automated solution.

name: Kindo
description: Founded in 2010, Kindo began as a solution to a common parenting challenge: to make healthy school lunches easy for families and effortless for schools. Since then, it has evolved to become New Zealand's leading school payments platform, supporting lunches, payments and e-commerce for schools nationwide.

name: Kry10
description: The Kry10 Operating System (KOS) and Platform is a new operating system and management service aimed directly at connected devices. Unlike alternatives, it is highly secure, providing ultimate protection from attack. Founded by Boyd Multerer, ex-Microsoft and the technical brains behind the Xbox live architecture, the platform is designed for industrial systems, infrastructure, transport, and government.

name: LawVu
description: LawVu is an NZ mid-market SaaS company selling software servicing; matters, contracts, insights and other capabilities to in-house legal teams primarily in NZ, the UK and US. The cloud-based platform was looking to take advantage of the movement of corporate functions towards digital adoption, giving legal departments a clearer view of operations and providing a complete end-to-end system.

name: Mint Innovation
description: Every year, more than US$80 billion worth of valuable metals are lost to waste, with electronic and automotive waste accounting for around half of that total. Recognising both the challenge and opportunity, Mint Innovation developed the world's first biorefinery using their patented biometallurgical process to sustainably extract critical metals (such as gold, palladium and copper) from electronic waste and other feedstocks, helping build more resilient and circular supply chains for the materials our world increasingly depends on.

name: Miruku
description: Miruku is developing a novel technique for producing alternative dairy proteins through a molecular farming platform. Their approach involves growing proteins directly in plants, where cells are recruited as mini-factories to produce proteins, fats, and sugars that are normally only sourced from animals. The four founding team members are considered to be among the best in the world in their fields, both scientifically and commercially.

name: Open
description: Open is a digital insurance platform that provides the backend technology for brands to offer embedded insurance products to their customers. The company aims to make insurance simple, accessible and affordable for everyone.

name: ParkHelp
description: ParkHelp (originally Parking Sense) offered parking guidance and curbside management technology. The company had expanded globally and developed its product portfolio as it positioned itself as a leader in digitising the global parking industry.

name: Portainer.io
description: Portainer provides an operational toolset to simplify the use of container orchestration systems. Its products give enterprise IT and operational technology teams a single control plane to deploy, govern and update container workloads across multi-cluster, edge and air-gapped environments. The software has had remarkable engagement around the world, with over 2b pulls and 500k developers and IT engineers using it monthly (and growing).

name: PowerbyProxi
description: PowerbyProxi first began as a spin-out from the University of Auckland’s Engineering School, built on nearly three decades of wireless power research, and successfully commercialised its technology across industrial and consumer applications. Heralded as a developer of the world’s most advanced and safest wireless power system, it was acquired by Apple in October 2017.

name: Re-Leased
description: Built for owners, operators, and investors, Re-Leased streamlines property management with intelligent workflows that save time, reduce costs, and minimise risk, while providing a single source of truth across portfolios with instant visibility into performance, compliance, and operations.

name: RespirAq
description: RespirAq is a MedTech company developing a humidification system for hospital ventilators. Patients who rely on ventilators need humidified air to protect and maintain their airways, but typically systems depend on external water-based components and complex setups. RespirAq’s Active Humidifier removes the need for added water by using a smart membrane and integrated heating to manage moisture directly, improving reliability in critical care settings — an innovation that has since earned U.S. FDA Breakthrough Device Designation.

name: RosterLab
description: Born from the founders PhD’ research, RosterLab’s AI-driven engine is revolutionising hospital rostering. Its SaaS solution uses a proprietary algorithm to streamline staff scheduling, managing over 50 rules simultaneously (incl. union regulations, staff preferences, and skill sets), to reduce rostering time by up to 90%. By freeing senior physicians from admin and prioritising staff preferences, RosterLab enables its customers to unlock improved efficiency and staff retention, and reduce burnout.

name: Solve
description: Solve provides enterprises with a real-time data warehousing and management solution which can be hosted in the customer’s own cloud, acting as a single source of truth, reconciling all of the customer engagement and touchpoints as well as providing audit trails for all database changes.

name: Static Technologies
description: Static Technologies is a New Zealand FinTech startup taking an offensive approach to fraud and scams. While conventional tools detect phishing and scam campaigns after the fact, Static intervenes while an attack is still running, disrupting criminal operations and generating actionable intelligence so organisations can stop losses before money moves. The platform focuses on the early stages of an attack, the window that carries most of the damage and the one traditional fraud and cyber tools tend to miss. It is purpose-built for the institutions fraudsters impersonate to gain legitimacy: banks, telcos and government agencies. Static works across New Zealand and Australia and is expanding into North America.

name: SupaHuman
description: SupaHuman has developed an AI compliance and authoring platform for vocational education providers. It codifies each provider's way of working to generate audit-defensible assessment and moderation materials, keeps them compliant as standards change, and gives educators more time to focus on better learner outcomes.

name: Tectrax
description: Tectrax has developed an electronic amphibious system for the aluminium boat market. The company partners worked with NZ’s leading boat builders to fit amphibious systems to aluminium or fibre-glass hulls, allowing the company to leverage OEM sales channels, give boat owners access to amphibious technology without changing brands, and showcase NZ boat manufacturers in international markets.

name: Timely
description: Timely is a specialist provider of appointment management and point of sale systems targeted at the beauty industry. EverCommerce, a US-based service commerce platform, saw the opportunity to build out their Fitness and Wellness portfolio through a bolt-on acquisition of Timely in 2021.

name: TracPlus
description: Built on 20 years of experience delivering tracking, telemetry, and operational intelligence to mission-critical environments, TracPlus provides aerial firefighting teams with a real-time view of aircraft, drops, and operations. With a strong focus on safety, efficiency, and precision, it helps wildfire agencies coordinate faster and respond with confidence.

name: TradeMe
description: Founded in 1998, TradeMe was a pioneer of NZ’s online C2C marketplace and online customer acquisition and endures as a dominant local platform and player. It was sold to Fairfax Media in 2006 for $750 million.

name: Tradify
description: Tradify was founded by then-tradie Curtis Bailey, who was frustrated by the paperwork involved in running a trade business. The platform simplifies essential workflows including quoting, invoicing, job tracking, and payments, making it easier to manage core business tasks and focus on the work itself. It was sold to the Access Group in 2024.

name: Unleashed Software
description: Unleashed provides manufacturing companies with tools that help them streamline operations and manage inventory. Founded in 2009, the company now has over 2,000 customers in key markets – NZ, AUS, the US and UK. In 2020, the company was acquired by Access Group, a leading provider of business management software to mid-sized UK companies.

name: Vend
description: Shortly after the first iPad came out, Vaughan Fergusson recognised the opportunity to leverage the hardware as a Point of Sale (POS) solution, thus launching cloud POS software company Vend. As a specialist provider of a cloud based retail system, Vend became well established globally with over 11,000 clients in 140 countries (as at 2016).

name: Wellumio
description: Wellumio is developing a revolutionary imaging technology that harnesses the power of nuclear magnetic resonance for communities that are least able to access MRI. The company's first product, Axana, is a portable brain scanning device that enables paramedics and first responders to rapidly identify and characterise stroke in patients. The Wellumio team brought deep domain expertise and prior startup experience, an ideal blend of skills befitting the company’s needs. Both founders had previously started companies in relevant industries and had worked together for a number of years prior.

name: ZeroJet
description: ZeroJet is creating the world’s first turnkey electric jet propulsion unit for boats. Doing much more than electrifying marine propulsion, its fully enclosed electric jet propulsion system improves safety by eliminating exposed propellers, enhances usability through quieter operation, and delivers strong performance while reducing environmental impact.

description: AI Clearing provides AI powered monitoring of infrastructure projects using drone data for fast progress and quality insights.

name: Celestial AI
description: Celestial AI was founded in 2020 by semiconductor industry veterans Dave Lazovsky, founder and CEO of Intermolecular, Inc. (NASDAQ: IMI) and Preet Virk (Macom, Mindspeed Technologies) who realized early on that artificial intelligence (AI) and machine-learning workloads would quickly become a data movement problem rather than a compute-limited problem for data centers. To solve this issue, Celestial’s CTO Phil Winterbottom (ex-Bell Labs, co-founded Entrisphere, Gainspeed) developed “Photonic Fabric”, an advanced optical interconnect technology designed to meet the growing demand for larger bandwidths in data centers. Unlike other photonic solutions, it delivers data directly to the point of compute on the silicon, offering >1.5 Tbit/s/mm2 package bandwidth (25X greater than CPO) and 10X lower latency. With high reach, protocol adaptability, and compatibility with standard interfaces, it outperforms electrical interconnects, enabling the connection and disaggregation of more servers while supporting latency-sensitive applications with remote memory usage. Additionally, its integration with high thermal design power ASICs sets it apart from traditional CPO technology. The company’s investors include Koch Disruptive Technologies, Xora Innovation, the early stage investment vehicle of Temasek, IAG Capital Partners, The Engine, Samsung Catalyst, Porsche SE, IMEC.xpand and others.

description: With the growing complexity of industrial data, efficiently processing and analyzing multistructural information has become a critical challenge. Emerging Generative AI (GenAI), particularly advanced Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) technology, offers powerful solutions for handling diverse data types and modalities, enabling context-aware insights. name: Cyllene Therapeutics
description: Cyllene Therapeutics is developing next-generation precision genetic medicines for prevalent chronic diseases using its proprietary non-replicative Herpes Simplex Virus 1 (nrHSV-1) HERMES platform, which enables safe, targeted, and durable transgene expression in peripheral neurons. The company's initial focus is on underserved bladder and neuro-urology disorders with high unmet medical need, with its lead programme EG110A currently in clinical development as the first non-replicative herpes vector-based genetic medicine evaluated in humans. Cyllene Therapeutics is headquartered in Paris, France, and is backed by an experienced investor syndicate including Andera Partners, Bpifrance, SCI, GordonMD, among others.

name: DISCO Pharmaceuticals
description: DISCO employs a disruptive proteomics technology to map the surfaceome of cancer cells and develop first-in-class cancer drugs. With the advent of new cell-surface, target-directed therapeutic modalities, it is critical to ramp up the discovery of meaningful targets. DISCO does so by comprehensively identifying druggable targets and protein communities (i.e., different proteins that form nanoscale organizations on a cell), across the entire cancer cell surface at scale, thus uncovering crucial new information that neither genome nor transcriptome sequencing can provide. By knowing which proteins are truly present on the cell surface, and how they are associated within protein communities, DISCO can design highly specific binders, boosting expected efficacy and reducing side effects. DISCO is backed by world leading life sciences investors including M Ventures, Sofinnova Partners, Panakes Partners and AbbVie Ventures.

By putting DNA synthesis back in the lab, DNA Script aims to transform life sciences research through innovative technology that gives researchers unprecedented control and autonomy. The Company’s technology has the potential to greatly accelerate the development of new therapeutics, sustainable chemicals production, improved crops as well as data storage.

Iktos’ proprietary and innovative technology is based on generative deep learning models, which allow, from existing data, to design optimized molecules in silico to meet all the success criteria of a small molecule discovery. Iktos is the only company to offer generative modeling with built-in synthetic accessibility for successful drug discovery and has already validated its technology through more than 50 collaborations with pharmaceutical and biotech companies such as Chiesi Group, Galapagos, Janssen, Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, Teijin, Ono Pharmaceuticals, Pfizer, Servier, UCB, etc.

name: ImmuneBridge
description: ImmuneBridge is developing the next generation of allogeneic cellular medicines, starting with NK cell-based immunotherapies. ImmuneBridge’s proprietary expansion technology amplifies cord blood-derived immune stem cells while maintaining full immune multipotency—to create a consistent and abundant cellular source for immunotherapies. Based in San Francisco, ImmuneBridge is led by Nina Horowitz, CEO and Rui Tostoes, CTO and backed my M Ventures, Insight Partners, NFX, One Way Ventures, LongGame, T.Rx Capital and others.

name: Immunitas
description: Immunitas is a clinical stage precision immunotherapy company committed to discovering and developing novel, differentiated treatments for patients with cancer. A focus on human data, combined with fully integrated internal R&D capabilities and parallel discovery efforts, allows Immunitas to start with and stay closer to the most relevant and translatable biology for patients, accelerating the timeline from discovery to the clinic. The Immunitas discovery engine combines deep expertise in single-cell genomics with customized machine learning approaches to elucidate immune cell populations that are key actors in immuno-oncology. The company was founded by Longwood Fund with leading scientists from Dana-Farber, MGH, the Broad, and MIT. Since being founded in 2019, Immunitas has raised a total of $97 million in venture funding from a strong syndicate of investors including Agent Capital, Alexandria Venture Investments, Evotec, Leaps by Bayer, Longwood Fund, M Ventures, Medical Excellence Capital, and Novartis Venture Fund.

name: Immunorizon
description: Immunorizon is developing conditionally activated Tumor-Restricted T-and NK-Cell Engagers for cancer therapy. The company extends its pipeline and differentiate by using tri-specific constructs with additional tumor associated antigens and diverse engagers with both T-cells and NK-cells.

name: iOmx Therapeutics
description: iOmx Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company focused on developing first-in-class cancer immunotherapies addressing novel immune checkpoints hijacked by cancer cells. Utilizing its iOTarg™ high-throughput screening platform, iOmx has identified a number of proprietary tumor-associated next-generation immune checkpoints and is advancing a preclinical stage pipeline of promising drug candidates that have the potential to address cancers that are resistant to current immunotherapies. The company’s lead program IMT-07 targets SIK3, an immune protective kinase in multiple solid tumors; the IMT-18 program is a first-in-class antibody designed to inhibit IGSF11, an immune checkpoint in PD1/PD-L1-resistant tumors. Founded in 2016 based on the work of its scientific founders Philipp Beckhove, MD, and Nisit Khandelwal, Ph.D., conducted at the German Cancer Research Center, iOmx is backed by international venture capital investors, such as Wellington Partners, Sofinnova Partners and M Ventures as well as MIG Capital and Athos Service. iOmx is based in Martinsried/Munich, Germany.

name: iOnctura
description: iOnctura is a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focusing on novel therapeutics to treat tumors burdened by stroma and immune mediated resistance. Company’s pipeline consists of two clinical stage small molecule programs against PI3kd and ATX and multiple preclinical programs. iOnctura is supported by a world renowned scientific advisory board and, with its access to CRT’s drug discovery labs and network of academic collaborators, is well-positioned to rapidly establish novel combination therapies in the field of cancer immunology. Headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, iOnctura was founded by M Ventures in June 2017.

description: IonKraft develops innovative plasma-based barrier coatings that can replace non-recyclable barrier solutions and enable a fully circular economy in the packaging industry. Furthermore, the barrier technology can provide sufficient protection to allow the incorporation of recycled materials into packaging for sensitive, food, or cosmetics products.

The company is headquartered in San Francisco, CA. For more information, visit www.kivubioscience.com.

name: LabGenius
description: LabGenius Therapeutics ("LabGenius") is a drug discovery company pioneering the discovery of next-generation therapeutic antibodies. The company’s discovery platform, EVA™, integrates several cutting-edge technologies drawn from the fields of artificial intelligence, robotic automation and synthetic biology. While EVA™ is both modality and format-agnostic, LabGenius' internal pipeline is focussed on the development of selectivity-enhanced antibodies for the treatment of solid tumours. The company's novel approach is delivering a pipeline of antibody therapeutics with best-in-class killing profiles.

name: Lightcast
description: Lightcast Discovery aims to unleash new capabilities within the single-cell analysis field by developing a more accessible, scalable, and flexible platform for scientists in basic, translational, and applied research. These capabilities will empower new biological discoveries and accelerate the development of novel drugs, therapies, and biologics. Founded in 2019 and based in Cambridge, UK, Lightcast has invented a technology that uses light to control picolitre-scale droplets for functional analysis of individual cells, which can then be moved to other platforms for further interrogation.

Lumiode offers a fully-integrated wafer-level manufacturing process that will ultimately enable the low-cost production for large-scale consumer and industrial applications.

name: Medisafe
description: Medisafe is the personalized medication management platform addressing all major causes of non-adherence. Medisafe’s cloud-based mobile platform personalizes content, resources and interventions — such as educational videos, coupons and motivational messages — based on each user's regimen, condition and specific circumstance. Medisafe fosters collaboration between patients, their loved ones and healthcare professionals through caregiver tools and reports, and helps the care continuum improve health outcomes and sustain quality care initiatives.

description: MemryX Inc. is a fabless semiconductor company that designs edge AI processing solutions powered by a proprietary compute-at-memory technology and dataflow architecture. MemryX has headquarters in Ann Arbor, MI, with offices in Bangalore, India, Taipei and Hsinchu, Taiwan.

name: Metalenz
description: Metalenz is a fabless semiconductor optics company on a mission to revolutionize optical sensing and empower billions of devices with new information. Metalenz is using metasurface technology built on foundational research from the Capasso Lab at Harvard University. Marking the beginning of this revolutionary optical technology in real-world devices, Metalenz launched meta-optics into consumer devices for the first time in 2022 in a range of consumer devices through its partnership with global semiconductor manufacturing leader STMicroelectronics. Metalenz is headquartered in Boston, MA.

name: Mosa Meat
description: Mosa Meat is set on the mission to create an affordable, reliable, and secure supply of meat products without slaughtering livestock. Mosa Meat’s technology development centers around widely deployed bioengineering techniques to develop an end-to-end industrial process for cultured meat production. Mosa Meat is focused, initially on developing nutricous and tasty cultured beef products with a commercially viable cost structure. Mosa Meat was co-founded in 2016 as a spin-off company from Maastricht University by Peter Verstrate and Prof. Mark Post, who in 2013 presented and cooked the world’s first cultured beef burger in London.

name: Multitude
description: Multitude is a clinical-stage ADC-focused platform company founded by successful serial entrepreneurs. Multitude's competitive advantage in developing industry leading ADCs is based on two proprietary platform technologies: MabArrayTM , an antibody platform for discovering novel cell surface tumor targets to build first-in-class ADCs, and T1000, a novel linker/payload technology for developing ADCs with a highly favorable balance of bystander effect, potency, and toxicity. The powerful synergy derived from combining MabArrayTM and T1000 enables Multitude to build an atlas of ADCs that has the potential to treat malignancies with high unmet needs and achieve higher and more durable responses. Multitude based in Shanghai and is backed by prominent investors including Northern Light Venture Capital, Co-win Ventures, Loyal Valley Capital, and M Ventures

name: NovoLINC
description: NovoLINC was co-founded by Dr. Ning Li, Prof. Sheng Shen, and Dr. Rui Cheng. The team recognized early on that the ever-increasing performance and power requirements of electronic chipsets were leading to enormous heat generation. Advancements in thermal interface solutions had not kept pace, making thermal management a critical bottleneck in efficient cooling and effective heat dissipation, especially as AI datacenters transition to liquid cooling. To address this issue, NovoLINC's CTO Dr. Rui Cheng developed a breakthrough nanostructured composite thermal interface material at Carnegie Mellon University that significantly advances thermal performance beyond traditional materials. Their solution reduces thermal resistance to an industry-record low (<1 mm²·K/W), offering outstanding thermal performance and reliability for cooling high-power electronics such as CPUs and GPUs. With its unique design, it enables sustainable scaling of semiconductor and data center industries. The company's investors include M Ventures, Foothill Ventures, and TDK Ventures.

name: NRG Therapeutics
description: NRG Therapeutics is developing first-in-class, oral, small molecule neuroprotective therapeutics targeting mitochondrial dysfunction and neuroinflammation for treatment of neurodegenerative and peripheral diseases. Its lead program reduces mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) formation to restore mitochondrial function. The program has broad potential with initial focus on ALS and PD and will enter the clinic in 2025. NRG is headquartered in the UK and supported by experienced biotech investors, including M Ventures, SV Health Investors’ Dementia Discovery Fund, British Business Bank, Novartis Venture Fund, Criteria BioVentures, Omega Funds, Brandon Capital and Parkinson’s UK.

name: Nucleai
description: Nucleai’ technology leverages spatial AI-driven algorithmics to analyze and interpret complex cellular interactions in a patient’s biopsy, translating them into actionable insights that can accelerate the development of life-saving treatments and diagnostics. Nucleai's platform ingests images from various modalities (H&E, IHC, multiplex immunofluorescence, and spatial transcriptomics), conducts advanced spatial analysis, and delivers actionable insights. These insights optimize biomarker scoring, determine biomarker prevalence and mechanism of action (MoA), and predict response to therapy, revolutionizing our approach to disease diagnosis and treatment.

name: Nucleome
description: Nucleome Therapeutics is decoding the dark matter of the human genome to uncover novel ways to treat disease. The dark genome holds more than 90% of disease-linked genetic variants whose value remains untapped, representing a significant opportunity for drug discovery and development. The Company has the unique ability to link these variants to gene function and precisely map disease pathways. Nucleome’s cell type-specific platform creates high resolution 3D genome structure maps and enables variant functional validation at scale in primary cell types, enabling the discovery and development of novel, better and safer drugs. The initial focus of the company is on lymphocytes and related autoimmune disease. Nucleome’s ambition is to build a robust pipeline of first-in-class drug assets, with corresponding biomarkers. Nucleome Therapeutics was founded by leading experts in gene regulation from the University of Oxford.

name: ObsEva

description: PictorLabs is a digital pathology company advancing AI-powered virtual staining technology to revolutionize histopathology and accelerate clinical research with the goal of improving patient outcomes. Led by a team with deep expertise in bioengineering, artificial intelligence, and health-tech product development, the Company is reimagining existing histopathology workflows, accelerating clinical and diagnostic results, and improving process sustainability. From a single unstained tissue sample, PictorLabs’ proprietary platform can produce an unlimited number of virtual stains that are indistinguishable from analogous chemical stains. PictorLabs is developing products that replicate standard of care stains and is creating specialized virtual biomarker stains for indications in which there is a large demand for novel and accelerated diagnostic tests.

name: Plexium
description: Plexium is a next-generation targeted protein degradation (TPD) company, leading the way in the rational design and discovery of monovalent protein degraders across a wide range of modalities. Plexium has built a comprehensive best-in-class TPD platform, powered by a proprietary high-throughput cell-based screening (uHTS) technology. Plexium’s next-generation TPD programs extend beyond the limited applications of Proteolysis Targeting Chimeras (PROTACs) and cereblon imids, unravelling the boundless possibilities of true drug-like protein degraders.

name: SEEQC
description: SEEQC is developing the first fully digital quantum computing platform. SEEQC combines classical and quantum technologies to address the efficiency, stability and cost issues endemic to quantum computing systems. The company applies classical and quantum technology through digital readout and control technology and a unique chip-scale architecture. SEEQC is one of the first companies to have built a superconductor multi-layer commercial chip foundry. Through this experience SEEQC has the infrastructure in place for design, testing and manufacturing of quantum-ready superconductors. SEEQC is based in Elmsford, NY with facilities in London, UK and Naples, Italy.

name: Storm Therapeutics
description: STORM Therapeutics (STORM) is a clinical stage biotechnology company developing novel therapies that inhibit RNA modifying enzymes (RME) for use in oncology and other diseases. There are more than 150 RNA modifications reported and approximately 300 RNA modifying enzymes which represent novel therapeutic targets. STORM has leveraged its first-mover advantage to establish a novel drug discovery and RNA analytics platform leading to the identification of novel targets and a proprietary pipeline of first-in-class small-molecule drug candidates for potential use in oncology, inflammation, viral infection and CNS diseases. The pipeline is exemplified by STORM’s METTL3 inhibitor, STC-15, which is currently in clinical development. STC-15 represents the first ever RNA modifying enzyme inhibitor to enter clinical evaluation in humans. Additional programs are planned for advancement into IND-track activities. Fierce Biotech named STORM as one of its 2022 “Fierce 15”, designating it as one of the most innovative, exciting biotechnology companies in the industry, pioneering novel drug targets.

name: TwoStep Therapeutics

name: UNISERS

The technology can provide unique chemical IDs of particle defects which can significantly reduce the time to find the root cause of on-wafer defects. The company aims to facilitate effective defectivity monitoring of individual process chemicals, high-purity components, and production tools across the entire semiconductor fabrication ecosystem.

name: 3E
description: Founded in 1988 and headquartered in Carlsbad, CA, 3E is a leading global provider of data-driven intelligent compliance solutions in the Environmental, Health, Safety & Sustainability space. The Company has a long history of innovation that has resulted in the development of differentiated and mission-critical data assets such as global regulatory content and a proprietary database of over 10+ million safety data sheets, 3,000+ regulatory lists and 30,000+ generic classes of substances. New Mountain identified 3E as it sits at the intersection of its multi-year deep-dive sector initiatives in the data and information services, software, chemicals, and EHS&S sectors.
