name: SuperDimension
description: superDimension developed minimally invasive pulmonology devices that enable the diagnosis and potential treatment of distal lung disease. The company focused on extending the reach of traditional bronchoscopy tools, allowing physicians to access and diagnose lung lesions that were previously unreachable and to identify disease at earlier, more treatable stages. superDimension was acquired by Covidien.

name: ConvertMedia
description: ConvertMedia developed technology that predicted a user’s likelihood to convert, calculated that user’s value, and purchased ads accordingly to maximize performance. By expanding the available inventory pool for advertisers, the company shifted the supply–demand balance and reduced acquisition costs. Built on advanced algorithms and spatial analysis, ConvertMedia’s Precognitive Ad Targeting (PAT) technology enabled advertisers to use the programmatic ecosystem more effectively for performance-based advertising. ConvertMedia was acquired by Taboola.

name: 3DV Systems
description: 3DV Systems, Ltd. developed three-dimensional video imaging technology that captured depth information and enabled users to control digital environments through body gestures. The company’s solutions were used in gaming, web conferencing, security, automotive, and robotics applications. 3DV Systems was acquired by Microsoft.

name: AudioCodes
description: AudioCodes Ltd. (NASDAQ, TASE: AUDC) is a leading provider of advanced voice networking and media-processing solutions for the digital workplace. The company enables enterprises and service providers to build and operate all-IP voice networks for unified communications, contact centers, and hosted business services. AudioCodes’ broad portfolio of products, solutions, and services is used by multinational enterprises and tier-1 operators around the world. AudioCodes was acquired by Active Communications Europe.

name: BackWeb
description: BackWeb mobilized critical web applications and content for mobile workforces and remote offices. Its solutions were commonly deployed to sales teams, field employees, mobile managers, and remote operations. Typical use cases included enterprise sales-force automation, CRM, e-learning and training, and human capital management (HCM). BackWeb went public on NASDAQ.

name: Card Guard
description: Card Guard, founded in 1986, designed, developed, and marketed telemetric and telediagnostic medical instruments. Its products included EEG devices, a lower-cost alternative to traditional Holter systems for short-term ECG monitoring, telemetry electrodes for real-time heart-rhythm transmission, and devices for detecting ischemia and arrhythmia during cardiac treatment. The company also developed fetal-distress monitoring technology and the Asthma Guard system, which enabled asthma patients to receive remote assessments of lung capacity and symptom severity. Card Guard went public on the Zurich SWX.

name: ClearForest
description: ClearForest Corporation provided text-driven business intelligence solutions that bridged unstructured text and structured enterprise data. By enabling both to be analyzed together, ClearForest helped organizations turn large volumes of contextual information into actionable insights. Its award-winning technology allowed Global 5000 companies to enhance their business intelligence applications by extracting relevant, high-value information from complex content sources. ClearForest’s customers included Kodak, Dow Chemical, Eastman Chemical, NASD, EDS, Boeing, the U.S. Air Force, Reuters, Dow Jones, and Thomson Financial. ClearForest was acquired by Thomson Reuters.

name: ColBar LifeScience
description: ColBar specialized in reconstructive medicine and tissue engineering, focusing on the repair of damaged human tissue including soft tissue, bone, and skin. The company developed a proprietary technique for purifying and transforming collagen to create a range of medical products. ColBar’s technologies supported applications in urology, gastroenterology, orthopedics, and cardiovascular care. ColBar was acquired by Johnson & Johnson.

name: Disc-O-Tech
description: Disc-O-Tech Medical Technologies developed expandable implants for minimally invasive orthopedic surgery. The company’s product development team of physicians, engineers, and product managers focused on identifying clinical needs and creating high-quality solutions that improved outcomes for both patients and surgeons. Disc-O-Tech was acquired by Kyphon.

name: Go Networks
description: GO Networks Inc. developed mobile Wi-Fi network solutions for service providers deploying large-scale campus and municipal wireless systems. Its technology was designed to improve coverage, capacity, and reliability in dense outdoor environments, enabling operators to offer wide-area broadband connectivity with fewer access points and lower deployment costs. GO Networks was acquired by NextWave.

name: Gteko
description: Gteko developed technology that enhanced and expanded automated and remote technical support capabilities, enabling companies to resolve customer issues more quickly and at scale. Its software automated routine troubleshooting tasks, reduced the need for live support intervention, and helped organizations significantly lower call-center costs while improving service quality. Gteko was acquired by Microsoft.

name: Optibase
description: Optibase was founded as a technology company in the field of digital video. The company went public in March 1999, followed by a secondary offering in March 2000, and has been traded on NASDAQ (OBAS) since.

name: RadCom
description: RADCOM specializes in assuring next-generation, high-capacity networks, including LTE, advanced LTE, 5G, IMS, and SDN/NFV. The company’s Network Intelligence solution provides end-to-end network visibility, from virtual tapping points through to actionable insights, helping operators monitor, optimize, and troubleshoot complex network environments. RADCOM went public on NASDAQ.

name: Retalix
description: Retalix Ltd. provided integrated software solutions for food and fuel retailers, grocery chains, convenience stores, and foodservice distributors. The company designed, developed, and delivered mission-critical software that connected operations across stores, headquarters, and distribution centers. Its platform enabled retailers and distributors to better understand customers, anticipate demand, enhance the in-store experience, and differentiate their offerings. Retalix’s solutions also supported targeted promotions and loyalty programs through advanced consumer-behavior analytics. Retalix went public on NASDAQ.

name: Optonol
description: Optonol Ltd. developed innovative ophthalmologic devices for the treatment of glaucoma. Founded in 1996 by medical practitioners, engineers, and entrepreneurs, the company focused on advancing minimally invasive solutions for improved patient outcomes. Optonol was acquired by Alcon.

name: Ubimo
description: Ubimo’s SaaS platform helps businesses understand and act on real-world consumer behavior, bridging the gap between the digital and physical worlds. Using advanced AI, the platform combines behavioral data from more than 150 million monthly active devices with one of the most comprehensive geographic indexes in the U.S. Ubimo enables organizations to embed strategic, location-based insights into decision-making, improving performance across shopper marketing, programmatic advertising, publishing, retail, and out-of-home media. Ubimo was acquired by Quotient.

name: Timeful
description: Timeful used an algorithmic approach to time management, combining big data, behavioral science, and AI to help people prioritize and make time for what matters most. Developed by experts in artificial intelligence, data science, behavioral research, and product design, the Timeful app enabled users to build better habits and manage their schedules more effectively. Timeful was acquired by Google.

name: SalesPredict
description: SalesPredict developed technology that helped companies increase revenue by identifying high-potential buyers and providing insights to accelerate sales cycles and improve conversion rates. Its platform combined machine learning, natural language processing, and predictive analytics, drawing on behavioral, firmographic, and demographic data to determine who was ready to buy, who might expand, and who was at risk of churn. SalesPredict was acquired by eBay.

name: Origami Logic
description: Origami Logic developed technology that helped marketing teams understand and improve their performance by showing what was working and what wasn’t. The platform unified and organized large volumes of marketing data across channels and platforms, allowing teams to search, analyze, and act on insights in real time. Global brands such as P&G, HP, JCPenney, Intel, and Omni Hotels relied on Origami Logic to measure impact and optimize their marketing efforts. Origami Logic was acquired by Intuit.

name: Convergin
description: Convergin developed technology that enabled service providers to accelerate their transition to IMS and service delivery platforms (SDP), while seamlessly orchestrating mobile, legacy, next-generation, and web-based services. Convergin was acquired by Oracle.

name: Check
description: Check, launched in 2008, developed a finance app that helped users stay on top of their bills and manage their money automatically. The app earned widespread recognition, including Android Editor’s Choice, Apple’s Best of the Year, CNNMoney’s “Cadillac of Money Management Apps,” and PC Mag’s “100 Best Android Apps.” Check was acquired by Intuit.

name: Mobile Access
description: MobileAccess developed distributed antenna system (DAS) solutions that provided reliable in-building wireless coverage. The company extended outdoor wireless signals indoors and distributed them through discreet antennas placed throughout a facility, improving coverage and capacity for carriers and enterprises. MobileAccess was acquired by Corning.

name: Dune Networks
description: Dune Networks was a fabless semiconductor company providing complete solutions for traffic management and non-blocking switching fabric. Its integrated circuits powered the core of Internet and storage platforms, meeting carrier-class requirements for scalability, next-generation services, and high reliability. Dune’s technology was used across enterprise backbones, access and aggregation networks, metro cores, national service provider networks, and high-end storage systems. Dune Networks was acquired by Broadcom.

name: Sansa Security (ex-Discretix)
description: Discretix provided embedded security technologies for consumer electronics devices, enabling secure video, payment, and BYOD services. Its products included hardware security co-processors and a broad range of integrated security applications designed to enhance device protection without compromising user experience. Discretix was acquired by ARM.

name: Cadent
description: Cadent developed digital products and services for restorative dentistry and orthodontics, including advanced intra-oral scanners. Its CAD/CAM technology replaced traditional plaster molds, enabling precise adjustments for bridges, implants, and prosthetics, and allowing clinicians to visualize treatment outcomes before procedures. Cadent was acquired by Align Technology.

name: dbMotion
description: dbMotion provided a solution that enabled healthcare organizations to securely share clinical information across different formats, systems, and locations. By unifying patient data from disparate sources, dbMotion helped clinicians make clearer, faster decisions and deliver safer, more coordinated care. dbMotion was acquired by Allscripts.

name: Aeroscout
description: AeroScout’s Visibility System used real-time location (RTLS), Active RFID, and telemetry technologies to deliver operational visibility and measurable business benefits. The company pioneered the Wi-Fi visibility market with the industry’s first Wi-Fi–based Active RFID tag and received recognition from leading analysts, industry publications, and awards programs. AeroScout was acquired by Stanley Healthcare.

name: WorkLight
description: Worklight enabled organizations to efficiently create and run HTML5, hybrid, and native mobile applications for smartphones and tablets using industry-standard technologies and tools. The platform provided a comprehensive and extensible IDE that supported maximum code reuse and per-device optimization, along with mobile middleware, management capabilities, and analytics to support large-scale mobile deployments. Worklight was acquired by IBM.

name: VideoSurf
description: VideoSurf developed an advanced video search engine that helped users search, watch, and discover videos across the web, TV, and mobile devices. Founded in 2006 by experts in search, multi-grid techniques, and computer vision, the company created technology that could visually analyze the content inside videos. By extracting detailed visual information that traditional video sites and search engines could not detect, VideoSurf delivered more relevant results and a significantly improved user experience. VideoSurf was acquired by Microsoft.

name: SuperDerivatives
description: SuperDerivatives provided cloud-based, real-time market data, derivatives technology, and valuation services for financial and commodity markets. Its live market data was available both in real time and as end-of-day independent market rates, supporting more accurate pricing, risk management, and transparency for market participants. SuperDerivatives was acquired by Intercontinental Exchange.

name: Neebula Systems
description: Neebula developed Service Availability Management software that improved IT performance and uptime by automatically mapping and managing business services rather than isolated infrastructure components. Built for SaaS delivery, Neebula enabled IT teams to move from siloed monitoring of servers, networks, storage, and applications to a unified view of end-user business services such as CRM, billing, and payments. Its proprietary technology created and continuously maintained a real-time service map across physical, virtual, network, and storage layers, helping organizations focus on what truly impacts the business. This business-aware visibility enhanced event management, accelerated problem isolation, strengthened change control, and delivered clearer service health insights. Neebula was acquired by ServiceNow.

name: ImVision
description: ImVision protected business applications at Fortune 500 companies from API-related attacks. Its NLP-driven anomaly management platform helped CISOs gain full visibility and control over their APIs by eliminating blind spots from code to production. The platform automatically identified, analyzed, and mitigated potential breaches, enabling organizations to secure APIs at scale.

description: Celeno provides high-performance Wi-Fi chips and software for demanding home networking applications. name: Iguazio

description: Neura’s Behavioral Intelligence Platform gives organizations real-world behavioral insights that elevate decision making and performance. Brands use Neura to build high-value audiences, enrich their CRM data, and trigger contextual engagements that drive better outcomes. The platform has also supported public health initiatives by helping decision makers monitor and contain the spread of COVID-19 and by enabling predictive test pooling through ViruScoreTM.

name: CyberMDX
description: CyberMDX is a leading medical cybersecurity provider that delivers zero-touch visibility and threat prevention for connected medical devices and clinical assets. Its scalable, easy-to-deploy platform gives hospitals unmatched insight and protection to ensure device uptime, patient safety, and data security. CyberMDX’s multidisciplinary team includes veterans of Israel’s elite cyber units, medical device specialists, and academic leaders in AI.

name: Optimal+ (now NI)
description: OptimalPlus provided advanced data analytics and real-time quality intelligence solutions for semiconductor and electronics manufacturers, helping global enterprises improve yield, reliability, and product performance. The company was acquired by National Instruments, where its technology continues to support software-connected systems for data-driven engineering and validation.

name: Anobit
description: Anobit developed advanced signal processing technology that significantly improved the cost, performance, and endurance of flash memory devices, enabling next-generation storage solutions. Founded by leading experts in signal processing, digital communications, and silicon design, the company became a key innovator in the global flash market. Acquired by Apple in 2011 and integrated as Apple R&D Israel, the company’s first R&D center outside the United States.

name: Ivy
description: Ivy is a community and business management platform built specifically for interior designers. Its intuitive tools help designers run projects, track finances, and manage clients with far less manual work. Created by designers for designers, Ivy replaces spreadsheets and paperwork with a modern workflow that keeps every project organized and every detail in sync.

name: ParallelM
description: ParallelM provided a fast, reliable path to AI value by automating the deployment, orchestration, and management of machine learning systems in production. ML in production is uniquely challenging due to its non-deterministic, continuously changing behavior, and without proper controls, inaccurate predictions can create significant business risk. ParallelM’s ML Ops Center pioneered the discipline of ML Ops by reducing the time and resources required to deploy and manage ML pipelines, ensuring they scale and perform properly. The platform helped organizations turn ML initiatives into a repeatable, optimized lifecycle, giving Ops teams visibility and control while allowing data scientists to focus on building better models. By combining code instrumentation, distributed data correlation, and ML-driven analytics, ML Ops Center monitored prediction quality in real time and drove corrective action. ParallelM complemented existing ML development tools and analytic engines. Acquired by DataRobot.

name: LiveU
description: LiveU is a pioneer in broadcast-quality live video transmission over cellular networks, enabling HD and SD video streaming from virtually any location worldwide. Its technology has powered coverage of major breaking news and global events, including the U.S. Presidential Campaign, the London Olympics, Hurricane Sandy, the Royal Wedding, the GRAMMY Awards, and the Super Bowl. LiveU’s solutions combine multiple 4G/3G, HSPA+, WiMAX, and Wi-Fi links to deliver maximum video quality and reliability. A leader in live video over cellular technology, LiveU was acquired by Francisco Partners and Israel Growth Partners.

name: Skycure
description: Skycure, acquired by Symantec, provided advanced mobile threat defense that predicted, prevented, and detected cyberattacks across device, network, malware, and vulnerability vectors. Designed to protect without compromising usability or battery life, Skycure enabled organizations to confidently embrace BYOD while maintaining strong security and control. Its dual-layer architecture combined an on-device module with cloud-based analysis to deliver continuous monitoring, intelligent threat response, and zero-downtime protection of critical resources. Skycure supported HIPAA and HITECH compliance and was trusted by numerous Fortune 500 companies.

name: Ventor Technologies
description: Ventor Technologies developed a valve prosthesis designed for “off-pump” implantation on a beating heart. Its proprietary design enabled easier placement, stronger anchoring, and improved hemodynamic performance. Acquired by Medtronic.

name: AutoNxt
description: AutoNxt is a Mumbai-based deep-tech startup building India’s first electric tractor with off-road autonomous driving capabilities. Its high torque-capable EV tractors deliver the same degree of operational performance for heavy-duty applications as conventional ICE-based (diesel) tractors. While India has taken several steps to reduce (on-road) transport emissions – with the transition to BS VI emission & fuels standards and the push for EVs – the off-road transport sector, which primarily comprises tractors (in agri and industrial use cases), has lagged. The outdated emission control technology for India’s tractors, coupled with the expected rise in the stock of tractors in use as agri mechanization continues apace, makes the segment ripe for electrification. As the only Indian company with electric tractors ready for commercial deployment towards large-scale B2B industrial use cases (e.g., solar panel cleaning and hauling biomass fuel for energy generation), AutoNxt is perfectly positioned to be the category leader in this space.

name: Beans.ai (100 Hundred Feet, Inc.)
description: Beans.ai is a California-based early-stage company building a complete last-mile logistics platform offering hyper-accurate mapping and location data, route planning and optimization, and fleet management services. Its AI-powered platform provides unmatched visibility at every step of the package delivery journey – from address verification and geocoding to route creation, sorting, scanning, and sequencing to dispatch, delivery, and reconciliation. The platform collects and processes data from multiple sources and provides delivery partners with proprietary geocodes to simplify parking, access, and delivery. Beans.ai seeks to resolve issues in the last-mile delivery market, such as undelivered packages and re-delivery attempts which exacerbate the operational and cash burden logistics players face. Saama invested in the Company at a pre-product, pre-revenue stage based on our conviction in the founding team, which had deep technical expertise in on-demand delivery logistics. The CEO had previously led the on-demand delivery and 3rd party integrations group at Google and had an exceptional understanding of the problem faced by enterprises and delivery companies.

name: BlueStone
description: Bluestone is India’s leading brand of high-quality, design-driven, fine jewelry and accessories with strikingly exquisite designs. In an industry-first move, the Company was the first to leverage an omnichannel strategy for selling jewelry by marrying the convenience of shopping online with the visceral trust of an in-store shopping experience. At the time of our investment, while the fine jewelry industry in India was booming, it suffered from a distinct lack of a superior customer service experience. Cognizant of this gap in the market, Saama invested in BlueStone’s vision of disrupting the jewelry buying experience through a tech-enabled business model. As a maverick of the D2C approach, the Company started as an internet-first brand and later reimagined the traditional jewelry store to offer an immersive and contemporary offline buying experience. Saama’s early conviction in Bluestone was rooted in the solid entrepreneurial mix of the founding team – with one of the co-founders being a successful serial technology entrepreneur and the other being a 5th-generation jeweler from the CKC Jewellers group (a 150+-year-old leading jewelry brand in South India). We have realized a partial exit, and the company plans an IPO over the next 12-18 months.

name: dRisk
description: dRisk is an early-stage venture dedicated to building a ‘risk-free’ investing ecosystem and arming retail investors with the power of hedging by simplifying options to cover their trades. Over the past two years, there has been an unprecedented influx of retail investors in India’s capital markets and a concomitant explosion of interest in riskier assets (e.g., cryptocurrencies and NFTs). While these newly minted retail traders seek education on downside risk protection, the sheer number and complexity of strategies available to trade options necessitate an in-depth knowledge of finance. Novice traders are, therefore, extremely unlikely to effectively deploy options as a risk rationalization tool. dRisk plans to leverage this opportunity by developing an easy-to-use de-risking solution that enables users to buy a cover for their trade, offering 100% coverage of their losses. As a platform that abstracts away from the complexity of options to democratize hedging for retail traders in the form of a simple trade cover, dRisk is well-positioned to successfully navigate the boom in India’s retail investing landscape.

description: Abcuro is a biotechnology company developing treatments for autoimmune and cancer indications modulated by cytotoxic T and NK cells that express the inhibitory immune checkpoint receptor KLRG1 (killer cell lectin-like receptor G1). The company is advancing ABC008 toward the clinic, a first-in-class anti-KLRG1 antibody designed to deplete cytotoxic T cells that attack healthy muscle tissue in patients with inclusion body myositis (IBM). The company is also advancing ABC015, an anti-KLRG1 blocking antibody capable of reactivating inhibited cytotoxic T and NK cells in the tumor microenvironment.

name: Aliada Therapeutics
description: Aliada Therapeutics is a biotechnology company working to overcome delivery hurdles in CNS drug development. Aliada is advancing a new generation of CNS therapeutics using its novel BBB-crossing Modular Delivery (MODEL) platform technology, which has been shown to efficiently transport a diverse array of therapeutic cargoes into the brain, resulting in enhanced downstream effectiveness and addressing the critical need for efficient and versatile delivery technologies for large molecules and oligonucleotides. The company was co-founded by RA Capital Management, Raven, Johnson & Johnson, and Johnson & Johnson Innovation - JJDC, with further investment from OrbiMed and Sanofi Ventures.

name: Arexera Therapeutics
description: Arexera Therapeutics is developing a next-generation RNAi platform leveraging divalent small interfering RNA (di-siRNA) for selective gene silencing throughout the brain and spinal cord for diseases of the central nervous system. The company is initially focused on Huntington’s disease, with programs targeting HTT and MSH3, and plans to initiate a Phase 1 study of its lead HTT-targeting program, ATL-101, by the end of 2026.

name: Attovia Therapeutics
description: Attovia is building a pipeline of biotherapeutics for the treatment of immune-mediated diseases. The company leverages ATTOBODY, its proprietary biologics platform, to generate first-in-class and best-in-class bispecifics and multispecifics with enhanced potency and tunable half-life.

name: Avilar Therapeutics
description: Avilar Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company pioneering the discovery and development of extracellular protein degraders. Avilar develops ATACs (ASGPR Targeting Chimeras), a new class of protein degraders that shuttle disease-causing proteins from circulation to the endolysosome where the unwanted proteins are degraded.

name: Bionyra
description: Bionyra is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing next-generation mono- and multispecific antibodies for severe immunological and inflammatory diseases. Its pipeline focuses on selectively modulating key immune pathways using multi-pronged biology and half-life extension technologies to enable deeper, more durable responses, with lead programs targeting atopic dermatitis and inflammatory bowel disease.

name: Bluebird Bio
description: At the heart of bluebird bio's product creation efforts is its broadly applicable gene therapy platform for the development of novel treatments for diseases with few or no clinical options. The company's novel approach uses stem cells harvested from the patient's bone marrow into which a healthy version of the disease causing gene is inserted. After being grown in culture, those cells are given back to the patient. bluebird bio's approach represents a true paradigm shift in the treatment of severe genetic diseases by eliminating the potential complications associated with donor cell transplantation and potentially presenting a one-time transformative therapy. Bluebird bio has two later stage clinical products in development for childhood cerebral adrenoleukodystrophy (CCALD) and beta-thalassemia/sickle cell anemia. The company is also applying its gene therapy platform to oncology through the development of chimeric antigen receptor T-cells in collaboration with Baylor University and Celgene.

name: BranchLab
description: BranchLab is transforming healthcare commercialization with AI-native technology that helps leading healthcare organizations and their agencies connect patients, providers, and caregivers to life-improving therapies and resources. Built for the evolving privacy landscape, BranchLab improves commercialization performance without relying on individual-level health information. By modernizing the industry’s technical infrastructure, BranchLab helps organizations operate more efficiently and responsibly, while enabling a healthier system for everyone

name: Carbon Health
description: Carbon Health is a modern health provider that is making high-quality healthcare more accessible to everyone. By combining advanced technology with expert care, they simplify access to a full spectrum of health needs – from acute issues to primary care, chronic conditions, as well as clinical research. Carbon Health has built a full-stack technology platform that enables their patients to completely customize and optimize healthcare delivery to meet their needs. Their technology allows them to operate more efficiently than legacy health providers, effectively lowering the cost of care. Carbon Health is removing traditional boundaries to make high-quality, transparent, and personal care accessible and affordable.

name: Character Biosciences
description: Character is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing precision medicines for polygenic diseases. Its pipeline includes programs in dry age-related macular degeneration (AMD), geographic atrophy (GA), and primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG). The lead candidate is a de novo–designed apolipoprotein A1 mimetic peptide, being developed as a potential first-in-class therapy for high-risk intermediate AMD.
location: 3 Second Street, Jersey City, NJ, 07302 1000 Marina Blvd, Brisbane, CA 94005

name: Click Therapeutics
description: Click Therapeutics, Inc. develops and commercializes software as prescription medical treatments for people with unmet medical needs. Through cognitive and neurobehavioral mechanisms, Click’s Digital Therapeutics™ enable change within individuals, and are designed to be used independently or in conjunction with biomedical treatments. The Clickometrics® adaptive data science platform continuously personalizes user experience to optimize engagement and outcomes. Following a groundbreaking clinical trial, Click’s industry-leading smoking cessation program is available nationwide through a wide variety of payers, providers, and employers. Click’s lead prescription program is entering into a multi-center, randomized, controlled, parallel-group, phase III FDA registration trial for the treatment of Major Depressive Disorder in adults.

name: Common Sensing
description: Common Sensing is introducing GoCap, a safer and more convenient way for diabetics to track and dose insulin. GoCap empowers patients by reducing the burden of manual logging, while providing helpful safety alerts and reminders. The aim is to connect patients, family, and care providers with better information feedback. By improving care engagement and motivation, GoCap holds the potential to improve quality of life for diabetics and reduce cost burdens for the health care system.

name: Curevo Vaccine
description: Curevo is a clinical stage company advancing a non-mRNA adjuvanted subunit vaccine for shingles with improved tolerability.

name: Curisium
description: Curisium is a healthcare technology and services company that provides scalable innovative contracting solutions with its blockchain-based platform. The Curisium platform uses cutting-edge blockchain and secure computation technologies to allow payers, providers, and life science companies to efficiently and securely engage in innovative, patient-centric value-based contracts.

name: Diagonal Therapeutics
description: Diagonal Therapeutics is a company advancing novel disease-modifying clustering antibodies that repair dysregulated signaling implicated in a range of illnesses with a lead program (DIAG723) being advanced in hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) and pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH).

name: Draig Therapeutics
description: Draig Therapeutics is a clinical-stage company with a mission to transform treatments in neuropsychiatry. The company is leveraging its founders’ unique scientific expertise in modulating the core glutamate / GABA pathways that play a critical role in neuropsychiatric diseases to advance a pipeline of groundbreaking therapies designed to address large unmet patient needs, including in Major Depressive Disorder (MDD). Draig is the Welsh word for ‘dragon’ and it reflects the company’s origins in Wales. The name and logo were inspired by this heritage, reflecting its scientific roots stemming from Cardiff University. Draig was co-founded by Cardiff University and SV Health Investors, which led the seed financing with ICG, and is backed by other leading healthcare venture firms including Access Biotechnology, Canaan Partners, SR One, Sanofi Ventures and Schroders Capital. For more information, please visit www.draigtherapeutics.com

name: Eligo Bioscience
description: By focusing on the in-vivo delivery of genetic cargoes to the microbiome, Eligo’s technology goes beyond traditional gene therapy and gene editing, expanding the range of addressable genetic targets. Through precise genetic modification within the human microbiome, this unique approach holds the promise of radically altering the course of numerous chronic and life-threatening diseases that are either triggered or driven by the expression of bacterial genes.

name: Empatica
description: Empatica has developed a versatile smartwatch and sensor platform that allows for medical-grade continuous health monitoring. Empatica's EmbracePlus wearable device is equipped with advanced sensors that allow for the remote collection of physiological data, giving researchers access to a vast range of raw sensor data and clinically validated digital biomarkers. Their sophisticated full-stack research suite allows to seamlessly conduct clinical research in real-world settings, helping to develop new digital endpoints and digital biomarkers.

name: Epicrispr Biotechnologies
description: Epicrispr is a biotechnology company advancing a pipeline of gene-modulating therapies, leading with treatments for neuromuscular diseases. The company’s proprietary Gene Expression Modulation System (GEMS) enables precise and durable epigenetic modulation of gene expression, unlocking first-in-class treatments for previously untreatable conditions. Epicrispr’s lead program, EPI-321, is in clinical trials for facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD).

name: Escient Pharmaceuticals
description: Escient Pharmaceuticals is a biotechnology company that is advancing first-in-class G Protein-Coupled Receptor (GPCR)-targeted drugs to address serious, unserved medical needs across a broad range of therapeutic indications. Focused on unleashing the therapeutic potential of specific orphan GPCRs, including the novel family of Mas-Related G-Protein Receptors (MRGPRs), Escient’s lead program targets MRGPRX4 for cholestatic and uremic pruritus. Based in San Diego, Calif., Escient is led by an experienced team of biotechnology entrepreneurs with specific expertise in GPCR drug discovery and development.

name: Evidation
description: Rooted in rigorous science, Evidation captures and analyzes passive, continuous behavior data to quantify health outcomes that more accurately reflect an individual's day-to-day experience.

name: Expansion Therapeutics
description: Expansion Therapeutics is a drug discovery and development company pursuing the vast potential of small molecule medicines for RNA-mediated diseases. Based on exclusive worldwide rights to groundbreaking research from the laboratory of Matthew D. Disney, Ph.D., at The Scripps Research Institute, Expansion has assembled the intellectual property, know-how, and proprietary enabling technologies and tools necessary to facilitate the creation of potent and specific small molecule binders of RNA. Through this unique platform, Expansion is building a portfolio of novel RNA-targeted drug candidates with activity across a broad number of disease indications. The company’s initial development focus is on therapies for patients with expansion repeat diseases who currently have limited and unsatisfactory treatment options. Expansion is based in San Diego, California and Jupiter, Florida.

name: Expedition Therapeutics
description: Expedition Therapeutics is a clinical stage biotechnology company developing novel therapies for serious inflammatory and respiratory diseases. The company’s lead program is a next-generation once-daily DPP1 inhibitor with first-in-class potential in COPD and first/best-in-class potential across a broad spectrum of other neutrophil-driven diseases.
location: Hong Kong, CN and San Francisco, CA

name: Fate Therapeutics
description: The Company’s first-in-class cell therapy products undergoing clinical development today utilize healthy donor cells, which are modified ex vivo using pharmacologic modulators, such as small molecules, to improve the cells’ biological properties and therapeutic function. The company is pioneering a revolutionary approach to cell therapy using renewable master induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) lines generated from a proprietary iPSC product platform to derive cell therapy products that can be delivered off-the-shelf for the treatment of a large number of patients. Fate Therapeutics is a public company headquartered in San Diego, CA, with a subsidiary in Ottawa, Canada.

name: Fulcrum Therapeutics
description: Fulcrum Therapeutics is a biotechnology company developing new medicines to deliver a new future to patients and their families by transforming gene regulation in disease. Fulcrum's therapies are based on modulating gene regulation via control of genetic on and off switches of disease genes. Fulcrum, headquartered in Cambridge, Mass., was launched by Third Rock Ventures in 2016 and named a "Fierce 15" company later that year.

name: GlycoMimetics
description: GlycoMimetics is a public, clinical stage biotechnology company focused on the discovery and development of novel glycomimetic drugs to address unmet medical needs resulting from diseases in which carbohydrate biology plays a key role. Using its expertise in carbohydrate chemistry and knowledge of carbohydrate biology, the company is developing a pipeline of glycomimetic drug candidates that inhibit disease-related functions of carbohydrates, such as the roles they play in inflammation, cancer and infection. "GlycoMimetics has enjoyed a very positive and productive relationship with SV. We have appreciated the opportunity to consult with functional area experts as well as to be in regular communication about the progress of our unpartnered programs. It’s great to have a chance to be ‘on the radar screen'." Rachel K. King CEO, GlycoMimetics

name: Glycomine
description: Glycomine is developing orphan drugs for serious rare disorders of metabolism and protein misfolding for which no other therapeutic options exist. The company's approach is to use replacement therapies – substrates, enzymes, or proteins – and to target those molecules to clinically relevant cellular compartments. The company is based in San Carlos, California.

name: Granite Bio
description: Chronic inflammatory diseases represent the most significant cause of death globally. Patients with autoimmune, inflammatory and fibrotic conditions are lacking efficacious treatment options. Granite Bio’s first-in-class assets are designed to target fundamental disease biology.

name: i2O Therapeutics
description: i2O Therapeutics is a biotechnology company developing safe and effective oral formulations of therapies traditionally limited to injections. Using an innovative ionic liquid technology, this platform leverages the benefits of protecting the drug cargo while also transiently enhancing permeation across the epithelial lining when administered orally. i2O is focused on creating the next generation of oral peptide and protein-based therapies.

name: Icosavax
description: Icosavax is focused on developing safe and effective vaccines against infectious diseases that address important unmet medical needs and reduce healthcare costs. The company was founded on breakthrough computationally-designed virus like particle technology, exclusively licensed for a variety of infectious disease indications from the Institute for Protein Design at the University of Washington. Icosavax is located in Seattle.

name: Imbria Pharmaceuticals
description: Imbria Pharmaceuticals’ mission is to translate our understanding of cellular metabolism into innovative medicines that improve the lives of patients with limited or inadequate treatment options. The company was founded by doctors and launched by an all doctor executive team motivated by the promise of bringing new therapies to people in need. Imbria is propelled by a deep scientific interest in cellular metabolism and the mitochondria, and is guided by both values and a code of business conduct built upon their commitment to always put the patients, families and communities Imbria serves at the forefront of all that they do.

name: Immune Design
description: The company's technologies are engineered to activate the immune system's natural ability to create tumor-specific cytotoxic T cells to fight cancer and other chronic diseases. Immune Design's clinical programs are the product of its two synergistic discovery platforms: ZVex™ and GLAAS™. Immune Design has offices in Seattle, Washington and South San Francisco, California. "We are very pleased that SV has decided to invest in Immune Design. Our companies share the vision of harnessing the immune system to discover and develop new immune-based therapies in a number of large human diseases in which both companies are interested." Carlos Paya President & CEO, Immune Design

name: Inozyme Pharma
description: Inozyme Pharma is a biotechnology company developing new medicines to treat rare disorders of calcification. These diseases are characterized by mineral imbalances, which lead to over calcification of soft tissues and under mineralization of bone. Founded in 2016 with technology licensed from Yale University, the company possesses a deep understanding of the biology of calcification which it is using to develop new medicines that have the potential to drastically improve the standard-of-care and change treatment paradigms. Inozyme’s lead candidate is an enzyme replacement therapy designed to treat calcification disorders of the circulatory system, bone and kidney for which insufficient treatment options currently exist.

name: KaloBios
description: Prior to its relaunch as Humanigen, Inc., KaloBios was a public biopharmaceutical company focused on the development of monoclonal antibody therapeutics to treat serious medical conditions with a primary clinical focus on severe respiratory diseases and cancer.

name: Korsana Biosciences
description: Korsana Biosciences was founded to reduce the burden of neurodegenerative diseases for patients and caregivers. In partnership with Paragon Therapeutics, Korsana has developed Therapeutic Targeting (THETA™), a novel blood-brain barrier-penetrant shuttle platform designed to enable dramatically higher drug concentration inside the brain and overcome the limitations of earlier shuttle technologies. Korsana is advancing a pipeline of innovative THETA-enabled therapies for neurodegenerative diseases, starting with KRSA-028 for the treatment of Alzheimer’s disease. Korsana Biosciences was founded in 2024 with a $25 million seed investment from Fairmount and Venrock Healthcare Capital Partners. In September 2025, the Company closed a $150 million private Series A financing co-led by Wellington Management Company and TCG Crossover Management, with participation by J.P. Morgan Life Sciences Private Capital, Janus Henderson Investors, Sanofi Ventures, Foresite Capital, and others.

name: Kymera Therapeutics
description: Kymera Therapeutics is a biotechnology company pioneering a transformative new approach to treating previously untreatable diseases. The company is advancing the field of targeted protein degradation, accessing the body’s innate protein recycling machinery to degrade dysregulated, disease-causing proteins. Powered by Pegasus™, a game-changing integrated degradation platform, Kymera is accelerating drug discovery with an unmatched ability to target and degrade the most intractable of proteins, and advance new treatment options for patients.

name: Latigo Bio
description: Latigo is clinical stage company advancing a pipeline of Nav1.8 inhibiting small molecules for both acute and chronic pain.

name: LAVA Therapeutics
description: LAVA Therapeutics is developing a proprietary bispecific antibody platform that engages gamma-delta T cells for the treatment of hematological and solid cancers. The company’s first-in-class immuno-oncology approach activates Vγ9Vδ2 T cells upon binding to membrane-expressed tumor targets. LAVA was founded in 2016 based on intellectual property originating from the Amsterdam University Medical Center. The company has established a highly experienced antibody research and development team located in Utrecht, the Netherlands (headquarters) and Philadelphia, USA.

description: Lumena Pharmaceuticals, acquired by Shire plc in June 2014, is a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to providing better treatment options for adults and children who suffer from rare and debilitating liver diseases and serious metabolic disorders. The company is focused on developing oral therapeutics to improve liver function, relieve disease symptoms and dramatically benefit patient health.

name: Lysosomal Therapeutics
description: Lysosomal Therapeutics Inc. (LTI) is dedicated to innovative small molecule research and development in the field of neurodegeneration, yielding new treatment options for patients with severe neurological diseases. Our strategy leverages the clinically-validated link between lysosome-based genetic disorders and neurodegenerative diseases to establish a unique and effective molecular platform for novel drug discovery. LTI’s lead program targets Gaucher-related neurodegeneration, Parkinson’s disease and other synucleinopathies.

name: MacroGenics
description: MacroGenics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on discovering and developing innovative monoclonal antibody-based therapeutics for the treatment of cancer and autoimmune diseases. The company generates its pipeline of product candidates from its proprietary suite of next-generation antibody technology platforms, which it believes improve the performance of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-derived molecules. The company creates both differentiated molecules that are directed to novel cancer targets, as well as "bio-betters," which are drugs designed to improve upon marketed medicines. The combination of MacroGenics' technology platforms and antibody engineering expertise has allowed the company to generate promising product candidates and enter into several strategic collaborations with global pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies.

name: Matchpoint Therapeutics
description: Matchpoint is a biotechnology company harnessing the power of covalency to discover precision covalent medicines to transform the treatment of immune diseases and other serious illnesses. The company's proprietary Advanced Covalent Exploration (ACE) platform integrates advanced chemoproteomics, machine learning and covalent chemistry library evolution. Matchpoint has an emerging pipeline of novel covalent medicines initially focused on immunology.

name: Medisafe
description: Medisafe is the largest medication management platform with over 7M registered users globally. Medisafe’s growth is rapidly accelerating as the healthcare industry turns to digital health solutions to support patients. • The Medisafe digital health platform delivers a next-generation patient engagement and medication adherence solution which leverages an AI data-driven personalization engine to improve health outcomes across a broad range of therapeutic areas with ecosystem integration and clinical validation.
location: Haifa, Israel and Boston, MA, USA

name: Memento Medicines
description: Memento Medicines is a privately-held biotech company developing biologic therapies for retinal diseases. Their lead program, MMT-205, is a bispecific antibody that activates Tie2 and inhibits VEGF, two clinically validated targets that play a central role in the pathogenesis of retinal and vascular diseases. MMT-205’s agonism of Tie2 simultaneously with inhibition of VEGF may improve upon the established efficacy of anti-VEGF monotherapies in the treatment of retinal diseases such as neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) and diabetic macular edema (DME). Memento Medicines was founded in 2026 with a $93M Series A financing co-led by Forbion, RA Capital Management and Avego BioScience Capital, with participation from Sanofi Ventures and Samsara BioCapital. name: Minervax

The company was established in 2010 based on research from Lund University and is based in Copenhagen, Denmark.

name: Mirador Therapeutics

name: Muna Therapeutics
description: Muna Therapeutics discovers and develops therapies that slow or stop devastating neurodegenerative diseases including Alzheimer’s, Frontotemporal Dementia and Parkinson’s. These disorders impact memory, movement, language, behavior and personality resulting in disability and death of millions of patients around the globe. name: Nucleai
description: Nucleai is committed to bringing the power of spatial biology to reality by providing pharmaceutical companies and clinicians with AI-powered image analysis applications. name: Nura Bio
description: Nura Bio is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing neuroprotective therapies for the treatment of a broad range of neurological diseases. name: Nuvig Therapeutics
description: Nuvig Therapeutics is a biotechnology company developing a recombinant, engineered Fc fragment (NVG-2089) that binds to type II Fc receptors and recapitulates the immunomodulatory effect of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg). NVG-2089 has completed Phase 1 in healthy volunteers and is advancing into a proof-of-concept study in Chronic Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyneuropathy (CIDP).

name: Odyssey Therapeutics
description: Odyssey Therapeutics is focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing the next generation of immunomodulators and oncology medicines. name: Omada Health
description: Omada Health is a digital behavioral medicine company that inspires and enables people to change the habits that put them most at risk for chronic conditions like heart disease and type 2 diabetes. Omada’s program combines proven behavioral science, the power of professional health coaches and peer groups, connected technology, and world-class design to deliver clinically-meaningful results.

description: OMass Therapeutics is a biotechnology company discovering medicines against highly-validated target ecosystems, such as membrane proteins or intracellular complexes. OMass is advancing a pipeline of small molecule therapeutics in rare diseases and immunological conditions, therapeutics that target solute carriers, complex-bound proteins, and GPCRs.

name: T-Therapeutics
description: T-Therapeutics is a next-generation T cell receptor (TCR) company spun off from the University of Cambridge. The company was created to harness the power of T cell biology, evolved over millions of years, to create safe and effective treatments for many cancers and autoimmune diseases. We combine world-leading expertise in mouse genome engineering, deep expertise in biopharmaceutical drug development, single cell genomics, machine-learning and structural biology, anchored in a culture of creativity and collaboration. We are developing ‘optimal’ TCR based therapeutics using our proprietary OpTiMus® platform, based on a fully humanized TCR mouse that provides an almost unlimited source of unique, antigen-specific human TCRs. These TCRs are directed at multiple target classes, many of which have never been worked on before. We are developing a pipeline of first-in-class drugs that will become transformative medicines, reshaping the clinical landscape for patients with cancer or autoimmune diseases.

description: Therini Bio, Inc. is a vascular biology company focused on developing novel therapies based on a deep understanding of fibrin and its role in driving pathological inflammatory processes initiated by loss of vascular integrity. description: Pearl is a fabless semiconductor company specializing in high-performance Reference Clocks and Timing ICs. Timing chips are critical components for all today’s electronica applications. description: Tomahawk Robotics is a premier defense technology leader specializing in AI-enabled common control systems and integrated communication networks that redefine human-machine teaming on the modern battlefield. Tomahawk is a pioneer in interoperability across the defense sector with its flagship Kinesis Ecosystem. Kinesis is an open-architecture, platform-agnostic software solution that enables warfighters to operate and coordinate a diverse fleet of over twenty uncrewed aerial and ground vehicles from multiple manufacturers through a single, intuitive user interface. Now fully backed by BigBear.ai's predictive data analytics, Pangiam transforms real-time camera data into actionable intelligence, enabling a frictionless world where people and goods move securely across borders, infrastructure, and secure facilities.

name: UbiQD

At UbiQD, we know that great technologies depend on great materials. Our patented quantum dots hold the key to unlocking low-waste, high-efficiency solutions for society’s most pressing problems. By developing dots that are safe, reliable, and, affordable, UbiQD’s solutions enable a new wave of revolutionary technologies. Through green chemistry and novel manufacturing techniques, our solutions replace capital-intensive alternatives. UbiQD is headquartered in Los Alamos, NM and we are licensing technology developed at leading research institutions, including Los Alamos National Laboratory and MIT.
